items.meaning_mnemonic: Set one <radical>evening</radical> on top of another and the stack of spent days behind you already counts as <kanji>many</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Tally</reading> stacks one evening on top of another and marks each with a 「<reading>た</reading>」, until the pile of spent days behind her is far too <kanji form="多">many</kanji> to count.
items.description: The look-alike is 名, meaning name. Both start with the same leaning crescent on top. In this kanji a second identical crescent sits directly below it, the very same shape written twice; in 名 a closed square box sits there instead.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> leans on the left, tucked behind it a little <radical>cocoon</radical>, sealed tight. Nobody else knows it is there. You grew the crop in the open, then kept one seed back for yourself: <kanji>private</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shi is the quiet one who keeps her own small field behind the house, and when anyone asks what she is growing in it she says 「<reading>し</reading>」 and closes the gate. Not rude, exactly. Whatever is in there is hers, and し is the only answer you are ever going to get.

items.mnemonic_text: A cord wound down a post: the younger, lower-ranked brother.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>younger brother</kanji> is kid number <radical>eight</radical>, so all he inherits is a thin <radical>slash</radical> of cake and a round of tired <radical>condolences</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A caterer called <reading>Tay</reading> only ever shouts 「<reading>てい</reading>」 when he hands the smallest plate to the <kanji>younger brother</kanji>, since the runt of the family always eats last.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Whoever pulls the <radical>arrow</radical> out of you and shuts it inside a <radical>hiding enclosure</radical> has done a <kanji>doctor</kanji>'s entire job.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway up the mountain trail a hiker catches a stray arrow graze, and the doctor in the group digs a first-aid kit out of her pack. The moment the antiseptic touches the cut the hiker yelps a sharp <reading>eek</reading>, and it echoes off the rocks as <reading>い</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (土-like legs) bounding forward: to run.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You break into a <kanji>run</kanji> because the <radical>earth</radical> baking under your shoes will not let you <radical>stop</radical> moving for even one second.
items.reading_mnemonic: Halfway up the mountain trail, the midday sun turns the dirt to a griddle. A hiker named <reading>Sew</reading> feels it burn through her boots, cannot stand still for even a breath, and sprints for the vending machine at the top, yelping <reading>そう</reading> with every stride.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Grabbing somebody by the <radical>ear</radical> with your <radical>right hand</radical> is the rudest way there is to <kanji>take</kanji> them anywhere.
items.reading_mnemonic: A teacher named <reading>Shu</reading> grabs the late boy by the ear with her right hand and hisses 「<reading>しゅ</reading>」 as she marches off to <kanji form="取">take</kanji> him to the office.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> at the left edge, beside a hide hauled off in one sheet — all <radical>skin</radical>, no animal left. Someone walked past carrying it and is already down the road. That man you point at and cannot name: <kanji>he</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hii is the little intake of breath you make when the man in the skin cloak goes past without a word — 「<reading>ひ</reading>」. By the time you finish it, he is round the corner. Every time you catch sight of him: ひ.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) who is already (市-like) senior: the older sister.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji>older sister</kanji> is the one <radical>woman</radical> in the house old enough to be sent to the <radical>market</radical> alone with the grocery money.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the market the <kanji form="姉">older sister</kanji> counts out the grocery money, and when the little ones tagging along beg for sweets she silences them with one sharp <reading>shh</reading>, 「<reading>し</reading>」.
items.description: Both put the woman 女 on the left, so the right side is the only tell. Here it is the market 市: a flat top stroke over a small box with one vertical dropping straight through. In the look-alike 妹 'younger sister' the right side is a tree shape instead, with two crossbars and diagonal legs that splay out wide.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stick of <radical>divination</radical> in the corner, a <radical>small</radical> mark beside it, a <radical>right hand</radical> scooping both up. He is the younger brother: not head of the family, so he gets the small share. Your <kanji>uncle</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shuku is that uncle, and he arrives every year with the same trick. He shuffles the sticks, throws them down, sucks his teeth, and pronounces 「<reading>しゅく</reading>」 as though it settles the matter. Nobody knows what しゅく means. He will not explain.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> on the left, a <radical>stick</radical> upright on the right with one <radical>slide</radical> of a stroke off it. That stick is a sundial, its shadow scratched beside. The sun moved on; the mark left behind is <kanji>yesterday</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Saku is the old gardener who checks his shadow-stick every dawn and then grumbles about how much better the light was 「<reading>さく</reading>」 — his one-word shorthand for the day before. Nothing is ever as good as さく was.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Daytime</kanji> is just the distance a <radical>ruler</radical> measures upward from the <radical>daybreak</radical> line to wherever the sun has climbed by now.
items.reading_mnemonic: Chuu, the loyal mouse with the tiny topknot, guards the sundial for the whole bright stretch of the day. When the shadow shrinks to nothing, he marks the middle of it with one proud <reading>ちゅう</reading>. That squeak is really just him biting a rice cracker, a single loud <reading>chew</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>altar</radical> stands on the left. Beside it, an <radical>eye</radical> lies flat above a line of <radical>ground</radical> — a portrait propped over the offerings. Somebody long dead looks back at you off that shelf: your <kanji>ancestor</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: So is the small catch of sound the incense makes when it takes light at the altar — 「<reading>そ</reading>」 — and for a second the eye in the portrait seems to move. One syllable, once a year, for the ancestor. そ.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>neck</radical> radical and the <kanji>neck</kanji> kanji are one and the same, so this review is a freebie.
items.reading_mnemonic: The face stretches up to the high shelf for a lost <reading>shoe</reading>, and its whole long <kanji form="首">neck</kanji> creaks 「<reading>しゅ</reading>」 as the two hairs on top brush the ceiling.
items.description: On its own 首 means the neck, but in compound words it usually shifts to head or chief, which is why it appears in words for a nation's leader or capital.

items.meaning_mnemonic: On the riverbank you tie a string of tin cans to the back of a toy <radical>vehicle</radical> and drag it down the muddy <radical>road</radical>. A wren, a bucket, and someone's lost sandal all snag onto the string, towed helplessly in a rattling line behind you. Everything hooked and <kanji>taken along</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The wren tangled in the string won't stop singing about it, chirping <reading>れん</reading> in a tiny outraged voice. Every time the cart yanks the line taut, it's like it's shouting <reading>wren</reading> at the mud.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>scribe</kanji> writes down everybody else's <radical>words</radical> and keeps <radical>oneself</radical> out of every single line.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> the tree spirit works as the forest's <kanji form="記">scribe</kanji>, carving everyone else's words into her bark with a bright 「<reading>き</reading>」 and never a line about herself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>ill</kanji> body is just a healthy one that <radical>sickness</radical> has bumped down to <radical>third class</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The mangy <reading>Bee-Owl</reading>, too <kanji form="病">ill</kanji> to hoot, gets bumped down to a third-class seat and coughs 「<reading>びょう</reading>」 all the way down the carriage.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Paper</kanji> is a mat of <radical>thread</radical> pulp beaten flat until it can hold a <radical>family name</radical> stamped on it in one clean press.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk <reading>Sheila</reading> beats the thread pulp flat, stamps a family name on it in one clean press, and hisses 「<reading>し</reading>」 over every finished sheet of <kanji form="紙">paper</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>hand</radical> nailing an <radical>omen</radical> to the door is going to <kanji>hang</kanji> it where everybody has to look.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa lands on that same hook, tilts his head at the empty <reading>sky</reading>, and screeches <reading>かい</reading> at the swinging poncho. It's the same rasp he gives anything left dangling in his sightline.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>hole</radical> cut so a lonely <radical>heart</radical> can see out of its <radical>cocoon</radical> is exactly what a <kanji>window</kanji> is.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same konbini, a raccoon dog crashes through the new opening chasing a dropped onigiri and skids across the tile. The clerk can only gasp 「<reading>そう</reading>」 — that flat English <reading>so</reading> of someone watching it happen with no better word for it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Grains of <radical>rice</radical> that <radical>stop</radical> inside the <radical>open box</radical> of your jaw were caught there by one <kanji>tooth</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: One shrine cat, nicknamed <reading>Shii</reading> for the hiss she makes mid-gnaw, clamps onto the bell rim and hisses <reading>し</reading> through the gap where a tooth used to be.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When your <radical form="疒">sickness</radical> makes you stagger down a narrow <radical form="甬">walled path</radical>, every wall you bump into adds more <kanji form="痛">pain</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A nurse follows you down the narrow lane to count the fresh bruises, but she only ever gets to <reading>two</reading>, 「<reading>つう</reading>」, before the <kanji form="痛">pain</kanji> makes you yelp.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Stiff <radical form="革">leather</radical> has to <radical form="化">change</radical> its shape around your feet before it can become a pair of <kanji form="靴">shoes</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading> the fire-breathing crow puffs little flames into your stiff new <kanji form="靴">shoes</kanji> until they soften, and he caws 「<reading>か</reading>」 each time a toe finally fits.

items.mnemonic_text: A horse (馬) waiting where trains stop: a station.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>station</kanji> is where a tired <radical>horse</radical> is swapped for a fresh one, set down every <radical>ruler</radical>-length along the road.
items.reading_mnemonic: The old horse-swap post on the line is a train station now, and its dome is built so the smallest sound comes straight back doubled. The stationmaster murmurs the stop's name once and it <reading>echo</reading>es down the platform as <reading>えき</reading>, loud enough that passengers dozing on the benches sit bolt upright.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Weave <radical form="竹">bamboo</radical> into four walls that face each other in a <radical form="相">mutual</radical> stare, and the space they guard between them is a <kanji form="箱">box</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Granny <reading>Sew</reading> stitches the four woven walls together at the corners, nodding 「<reading>そう</reading>」 at each one, until they close into a <kanji form="箱">box</kanji> with her own cat sewn inside.

items.mnemonic_text: Standing (立) by a tree (木) watching (見): a parent's love.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the edge of Sei's school field, someone has climbed a <radical>tree</radical> and wedged themselves to <radical>stand</radical> on the highest branch. They crane forward to <radical>see</radical> every second of the match without missing a kick. That straining figure, who won't leave until it's over, is a <kanji>parent</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: When the final whistle blows, they scramble down too fast and bark their <reading>しん</reading> — their <reading>shin</reading> — hard against a branch, then limp off still cheering about the goal.

items.mnemonic_text: A foot planted firmly: stop.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>stop</radical> radical and the <kanji>stop</kanji> kanji are identical in shape and meaning, so knowing your radicals well just handed you this one for free.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Sheila</reading> plants her foot flat on the ground, heel and toes dug in, and hisses 「<reading>し</reading>」 at anyone who tries to push her on, because that foot has come to a <kanji form="止">stop</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> who trails a step behind a <radical>samurai</radical> all day, carrying his sandals and his tea, is there to <kanji>attend</kanji> him.
items.reading_mnemonic: A servant called <reading>Sheila</reading> is so keen to <kanji>attend</kanji> her lord that she blurts 「<reading>し</reading>」 the second he clears his throat, already halfway to the kitchen.
items.description: Attend here means waiting on a master, not being present somewhere. In most compounds the character simply means doing or how a thing is done.

items.mnemonic_text: An old man's (耂) bent posture, deep in thought.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To <kanji>think</kanji> is to follow one <radical>old</radical> thought down a track so full of <radical>kink</radical>s that it catches and bends back on itself before it can go anywhere.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Koichi</reading> tries to <kanji form="考">think</kanji> one old thought through, but it catches on every kink in the track, and each time it bends back on itself he moans 「<reading>こう</reading>」.
items.description: This is 'think' in the sense of reasoning something out, considering, or weighing options, not 'think' meaning a hunch or a casual opinion.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> with an <radical>abrupt</radical> idea at two in the morning gets straight up to <kanji>make</kanji> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Struck by an abrupt idea at two in the morning, a tinkerer named <reading>Sock</reading> leaps out of bed whispering 「<reading>さく</reading>」 and starts to <kanji form="作">make</kanji> it before the idea fades.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> who plants himself in a house long enough to be treated as its <radical>lord</radical> has done nothing but <kanji>dwell</kanji> there.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Jude</reading> has not stepped outside his flat in ten years, and when the landlord knocks he just groans 「<reading>じゅう</reading>」 and goes on <kanji>dwell</kanji>ing.

items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) breaking through a levee (夬): a decisive break.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once the <radical>water</radical> droplet leaves the brush and the hooked arm that means <radical>decide</radical> starts to swing, both are past pulling back, which is what it is to <kanji>decide</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Calligrapher <reading>Ketch</reading> flicks the water drop off his brush and swings the hooked arm with a sharp 「<reading>けつ</reading>」; neither can be pulled back, so he has had to <kanji form="決">decide</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) directing an official (吏): to use, to employ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>use</kanji> a <radical>person</radical> the moment you make them your <radical>officer</radical> and start sending them out to do the errands you would rather skip.
items.reading_mnemonic: You make <reading>Shishi</reading> your officer and <kanji form="使">use</kanji> him for every errand you would rather skip, and he salutes with a sharp 「<reading>し</reading>」 before running off.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) with her own (台) fresh start: to begin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Nothing can <kanji>begin</kanji> until the <radical>woman</radical> running the ceremony climbs onto the <radical>pedestal</radical>, because the crowd only quiets down once it can see who is in charge.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Shino</reading> climbs onto the pedestal and hisses 「<reading>し</reading>」 at the noisy crowd, and only once it goes quiet can her ceremony <kanji form="始">begin</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When you <radical form="立">stand</radical> perfectly still and a puddle of <radical form="氵">water</radical> slowly grows around your shoes, nobody thinks it is rain, because you are having a big <kanji form="泣">cry</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The puddle gets so famous that people form a long <reading>queue</reading> to stand in it and <kanji form="泣">cry</kanji>, and each one squeaks a wet 「<reading>きゅう</reading>」 when it is their turn.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An elephant that swings its <radical form="牙">tusk</radical> through every roof in the <radical form="阝">village</radical> just for fun is plain <kanji form="邪">wicked</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Between the smashed roofs, the same elephant steals the baker's cookie <reading>jar</reading> and trumpets 「<reading>じゃ</reading>」 on the way out, because being <kanji form="邪">wicked</kanji> is hungry work.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Old</radical> dry <radical>grass</radical> is the only thing left to chew on, which is the plain taste of <kanji>suffering</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: He doesn't groan, exactly — what comes out is a strangled little <reading>coo</reading>, like a dove that swallowed a coin. The cashier doesn't even look up. She's heard that same <reading>く</reading> from every unlucky customer who trusted that shelf after dark.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>tree</radical> trunk with an angled <radical>chevron</radical> nailed on as a seat and a wad of <radical>grass</radical> for padding is the worst sled you will ever <kanji>ride</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Joe</reading> plonks onto the chevron seat of the tree-trunk sled, grass padding and all, and yells 「<reading>じょう</reading>」 all the way down on the worst <kanji form="乗">ride</kanji> of his life.
items.description: Besides getting on a vehicle, 乗 is also the math word for raising to a power, as in 2乗 for squared, a number climbing on top of itself.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) under a covering (覀): the essential point, needed.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Clamp a <radical>flat lid</radical> down over a whirling <radical>woman</radical> until only one arm fits through the gap, so the single thing she still grabs is what she truly <kanji>need</kanji>s.
items.reading_mnemonic: Dance coach <reading>Yo</reading> whirls under the clamped-down lid and shouts 「<reading>よう</reading>」 as her one free arm shoots through the gap to grab the single thing she truly <kanji form="要">need</kanji>s.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Each</radical> new person under your <radical>roof</radical> who did not pay a thing for it is a <kanji>guest</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: His ride up was a foul-tempered <reading>yak</reading> that refuses to leave the summit, planting itself by the machine like it's checked into a hotel. A guide radios down that a 「<reading>きゃく</reading>」 has arrived and shows no sign of ever checking out.

items.mnemonic_text: Two people (人) sitting on the earth (土) under a roof.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anywhere with a <radical>shelter</radical> over it is somewhere two people can <radical>sit</radical>, so that is where they <kanji>sit</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The person who settles onto that patch of earth is Zara, and the moment she sits she lets out a long, satisfied "<reading>ざ</reading>あ" of relief. Every time you see someone plop down here, you hear Zara's ざ.
items.description: Means "sit"; shows up in words about sitting down, seats, and taking a seat.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) relying on old (昔) favors: to borrow.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> walking off with what they need today and putting off paying it back until it feels like <radical>once upon a time</radical> is how you <kanji>borrow</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A drifter called <reading>Shack</reading> mumbles 「<reading>しゃく</reading>」 as he walks off with your ladder, since he only ever <kanji form="借">borrow</kanji>s things he plans to return once upon a time.
items.description: 借 covers renting as much as borrowing — money, an apartment, a bike, anything you take now and promise to give back or pay for. English splits borrow and rent; this kanji does both.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Two feet walking down a <radical>hill</radical> is the plainest way there is <radical>to descend</radical>, so the character just means <kanji>descend</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi treks up that same trail himself to restock the vending machine. When the last case slips from his arms and crashes down every step behind him, he just sighs 「<reading>こう</reading>」 — more <reading>cough</reading> than word — and watches it disappear downhill.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Let cement <radical form="固">harden</radical> around one <radical form="亻">person</radical> at a time, and every statue in the garden comes out a different <kanji form="個">individual</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The sculptor <reading>Coco</reading> knocks on each grey statue, and every one goes 「<reading>こ</reading>」 in a slightly different note, since no two <kanji form="個">individual</kanji>s sound the same.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) wound to its winter (冬) finish: to end.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When the reel's last bit of <radical>thread</radical> runs out just as <radical>winter</radical> arrives, both the sweater and the year reach their <kanji>end</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Knitter <reading>Shoo</reading> pulls the reel's last thread just as winter arrives, sighing 「<reading>しゅう</reading>」 because her sweater and the year both reach their <kanji form="終">end</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Fish swim straight at a shiny <radical form="金">gold</radical> <radical form="勺">ladle</radical> hung on a string, which makes it the laziest trick in all of <kanji form="釣">angling</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the riverbank, a fat cat named <reading>Chow</reading> sits by the line and yells 「<reading>ちょう</reading>」 at every fish that bites the shiny bait, because to him <kanji form="釣">angling</kanji> is just ordering lunch.

items.mnemonic_text: Money (貝) replacing (代) what's missing: to lend.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>lend</kanji> by handing your <radical>money</radical> to a <radical>substitute</radical> owner who stands in your place and must return every coin.
items.reading_mnemonic: You <kanji form="貸">lend</kanji> your money to <reading>Ty</reading>, a substitute in a crisp <reading>tie</reading>, who stands in your place nodding 「<reading>たい</reading>」 as he promises to return every coin.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Crossing <radical>water</radical> by counting the <radical>degrees</radical> the current pushes you sideways is how you <kanji>transit</kanji> a river.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto wades into the shallows with a sample door strapped to his shell, testing each stepping stone before he trusts it. Every plant of his foot lands with a flat 「<reading>と</reading>」, like a knuckle rapping a <reading>door</reading>, all the way to the far bank.

items.mnemonic_text: Bamboo (竹) matching (合) the right response: an answer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A written <kanji>answer</kanji> is a strip of <radical>bamboo</radical> that has to <radical>fit</radical> the question slot exactly, or the grader throws it out.
items.reading_mnemonic: Quiz host <reading>Toe</reading> slides each bamboo strip into the question slot and shouts 「<reading>とう</reading>」 the moment one fits exactly, the sign of a right <kanji form="答">answer</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Grass</radical> growing out of a roof in <radical>Kyoto</radical> means those tiles are about to <kanji>fall</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream, the fisherman who missed the splash finds the culprit lodged in the shallows: a plain grey <reading>rock</reading>. He nudges it loose with his boot, and it thunks back under the surface with a flat, hollow <reading>らく</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: Water (氵) cut down (咸) to less: to decrease.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull the plug in the bathhouse and <radical>all</radical> the <radical>water</radical> races for the drain, so the level can only <kanji>decrease</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Gen</reading>, the bathhouse attendant, forgets the drain plug every single night. He stands and watches the water sink lower and lower, muttering <reading>げん</reading> as though he is counting each inch it loses. By lock-up the great tub is a shiny empty pit and he is still there saying it.

items.mnemonic_text: Repeated breaths (可可) beside a yawning mouth (欠): a song.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>song</kanji> is what you get when your <radical>big brother</radical> starts a <radical>yawn</radical> so wide that it turns into a tune halfway through.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading>, the fire-breathing crow, lands beside big brother mid-yawn and caws a smoky 「<reading>か</reading>」 into his open mouth, so the yawn bursts into a full <kanji form="歌">song</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: Earth (土) piled ever higher (曽): to increase.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each new load of <radical>earth</radical> drops straight onto the layer that sat there <radical>formerly</radical>, so the mound rising past the signpost can only <kanji>increase</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every barrow of earth the <reading>zoo</reading>keeper tips onto the mound makes her groan 「<reading>ぞう</reading>」, since the pile rising past the signpost can only <kanji form="増">increase</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Strapping a <radical>dugout canoe</radical> onto a <radical>vehicle</radical> is a ridiculous way to <kanji>transport</kanji> a boat, and it works.
items.reading_mnemonic: The ferryman poling this contraption never learns anyone's name, so he calls every passenger the same drawn-out word as the wheels hit water: a long <reading>you</reading>. That same stretched syllable is the reading <reading>ゆ</reading>, hollered once as the crates lurch forward and the hull scrapes off from the bank.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>net</radical> of torn <radical>clothing</radical> and <radical>ten</radical> loads of <radical>earth</radical> is all that is left after a <kanji>demolition</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Grandma Kane's apprentice, a boy named <reading>Kai</reading>, surveys the wreckage and sighs the count out loud: <reading>かい</reading> — the third bell disaster this year alone. He says it flat, already reaching for the broom.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When every flower in the <radical form="原">meadow</radical> bows its <radical form="頁">head</radical> at once to beg the clouds for rain, that is one giant <kanji form="願">petition</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A grumpy <reading>gander</reading> waddles through the bowing flowers honking 「<reading>がん</reading>」 at each one for a signature, since no cloud reads a <kanji form="願">petition</kanji> with fewer than a thousand names.

items.mnemonic_text: A swaddled baby with arms out: a child.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This <kanji>child</kanji> kanji is a gift you already own, the <radical>child</radical> radical exactly as you learned it, without a single stroke changed.
items.reading_mnemonic: The <kanji form="子">child</kanji> runs at you wrapped in a blanket with arms thrown wide for a hug, squealing so loud you put a finger to your lips and <reading>shush</reading> 「<reading>し</reading>」 into the hug.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="丈">length</kanji> of a lawn is simply how far the giant shears can <radical form="乂">mow</radical> along the flat <radical form="一">ground</radical> before the grass runs out.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Joe</reading> the gardener will not buy a tape measure, so he mows the lawn shouting 「<reading>じょう</reading>！」 at every stride and tells you its <kanji form="丈">length</kanji> in Joes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Negative</kanji> is what one hard <radical>slash</radical> makes of the <radical>stick</radical> standing in the <radical>ground</radical> once even its last <radical>drop</radical> is wiped away.
items.reading_mnemonic: A critic named <reading>Foo</reading> slashes the stick standing in the ground, wipes away its last drop, and sniffs 「<reading>ふ</reading>」, his verdict always <kanji form="不">negative</kanji>.
items.description: Almost always a prefix: 不 flips the following word to its opposite, like English un- or non-, and rarely stands alone.

items.mnemonic_text: A marker at the top of the day: noon.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Held straight overhead at <kanji>noon</kanji>, a bone-<radical>dry</radical> shield throws almost no shadow, just one thin <radical>slash</radical>, because the sun is standing directly above it.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the school sports field, a gopher called <reading>Gordon</reading> only surfaces at noon, when the sun sits straight overhead and not one shadow falls to warn him. The moment the lunch bell blares <reading>ご</reading>, he bolts across the bright grass for the echoing hallways.
items.description: Two kanji crowd the same outline. 千, thousand, carries just one horizontal bar where noon stacks two, and it opens with a short flat tick instead of noon's longer left-falling slash. 牛, cow, is the nearer miss: its centre post pushes up through the top stroke, while noon's vertical stops flush against a slanted top and never breaks above it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Take the <radical>big</radical> figure — the <radical>person</radical> with arms flung wide. Lay one bar on top like a <radical>lid</radical>, so <radical>two</radical> strokes sit there, not one: his topknot pin. Grown and married: <kanji>husband</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Fu is the same breath out through the nose you learned from his father, inherited exactly — arms folded in the doorway, one 「<reading>ふ</reading>」, no further comment offered. Getting married did not change it in the slightest.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One <radical>mouth</radical> going at you for the <radical>seven</radical>th time has stopped being advice and become a <kanji>scold</kanji>ing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the konbini, the clerk everyone calls <reading>Sheets</reading> is still rubbing his ear from the crack of the cane. Every time the till beeps near him now, he flinches and mutters <reading>しつ</reading> under his breath, bracing for another scolding.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> that can talk a drawn <radical>sword</radical> back into its sheath knows perfectly well how to <kanji>seduce</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Backstage, Sho takes his bow, and the crowd gasps <reading>しょう</reading> in unison — one long <reading>show</reading> of a breath. He tips his tiny top hat, and that gasp is the only applause a magician his size ever needs.

items.mnemonic_text: An upright frame with pupils inside: an eye.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Nothing new to memorise here, because the <kanji>eye</kanji> kanji is simply the <radical>eye</radical> radical you have already seen, identical in shape and meaning.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Smoke</reading> drifts into the sideways box staring back at you, the eyelid snaps shut over both lines of pupil, and it splutters 「<reading>もく</reading>」, one sore <kanji form="目">eye</kanji>.
items.description: The look-alikes are 日 (day or sun) and 自 (self). 目 has three lines inside its upright box, splitting it into four stacked compartments. 日 has only one line across the middle, leaving just two. 自 is the same box as 目 but with a short slanted stroke added on top, like a finger pointing at your own nose.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You finish the job <kanji>by means of</kanji> whatever tool a helper holds out for <radical>using</radical>, because your bare hands are apparently not an option.
items.reading_mnemonic: The germ-shy clerk known only as <reading>E</reading> opens every door and jar <kanji>by means of</kanji> a gloved stick and squeals 「<reading>い</reading>」 whenever his bare skin nearly brushes anything.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) safe under a roof: peaceful and cheap.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a <radical>woman</radical> kneeling gracefully inside a snug little house, the <radical>roof</radical> pulled down over her like a blanket. Nothing can reach her in here — she is safe, the rent is nothing, everything is calm. A woman tucked safely under a roof is cheap and <kanji>peaceful</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: She's spreading sweet red <reading>あん</reading> (bean paste) on a bun, humming, utterly at peace. Every bite is cheap comfort — say あん and taste that calm.
items.description: 安 means cheap or peaceful, and shows up in words for low prices, safety, and being at ease.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One more pair of hands, and <radical>moreover</radical> all of their <radical>power</radical> as well, is what <kanji>help</kanji> actually means.
items.reading_mnemonic: When the cart sticks, <reading>Jo</reading> arrives as one more pair of hands, throws all of her power into the shove and grunts 「<reading>じょ</reading>」, which is exactly what <kanji form="助">help</kanji> means.

items.mnemonic_text: Power (力) worked in the rice field (田): a working man.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture a <radical>rice field</radical> stretching out under the sun, and the one person out there doing the heavy lifting. He bends his arm, flexes his <radical>power</radical>, and drags the plow across the paddies all day. Someone with that much power working the rice field — that's the <kanji>man</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The man out in the field takes a break and starts pounding out a rhythm on his empty water bucket: <reading>だん</reading>, だん, だん. Every man on the trail can hear that drumbeat and grins.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Charge a <radical>dollar</radical> for one cup of <radical>water</radical> and watch the whole queue <kanji>seethe</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A jumpy regular named <reading>Futz</reading> keeps mashing the button, muttering <reading>ふつ</reading>, ふつ under his breath every time the noodle water surges past the rim. Say his nervous little ふつ ふつ and the reading is stuck in your head with the foam.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Enough <radical>grain</radical> for every <radical>mouth</radical> in the village buys a whole season of <kanji>harmony</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Once the grain sacks hold enough for every mouth in the village, old <reading>Wah</reading> lets out a long 「<reading>わ</reading>」 of relief at a whole season of <kanji form="和">harmony</kanji>.
items.description: 和 alone usually means harmony or peace, but as a prefix on other words it commonly means Japanese-style - Japanese food, a Japanese-style room - describing where something comes from rather than describing peacefulness itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The part of the <radical>heart</radical> that goes about making new <radical>life</radical> is what we politely call <kanji>sex</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The nurse, exhausted, waves the form away and tells him to just <reading>say</reading> his name and leave — Sei straightens up and corrects her anyway: it's <reading>せい</reading>, properly stamped, thank you.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sprouting stalk</radical> coming up through your own patch of <radical>earth</radical> is the cheapest <kanji>happiness</kanji> going.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi the konbini king kneels by his own patch of earth to <reading>coax</reading> the little stalk up, cooing 「<reading>こう</reading>」 until it sprouts and his face fills with <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A blade cutting the way forward, in front of you.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A cow lowers its <radical>horns</radical> to the <radical>ground</radical> to guard the <radical>knife</radical> it dropped, so anyone crossing the yard by <radical>moon</radical>light has to freeze right in <kanji>front</kanji> of it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Long before sunrise, a monk sweeps the gravel yard out front and bows to the last of the moon. The other monks call him <reading>Zen</reading> because, whatever the hour, he is already there, and he answers to <reading>ぜん</reading> without looking up.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Water</radical> that pulls a <radical>banner</radical> straight out downstream is showing you exactly where the <kanji>current</kanji> runs.
items.reading_mnemonic: A boy named <reading>Ryu</reading> wades out too far, and the current takes him too. His voice trails off in a long <reading>りゅう</reading> as he's carried past the reeds and around the bend.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You can <radical>mow</radical> with a <radical>tree</radical> branch if you have to, but the <radical>pike</radical> is the one built to <kanji>kill</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, a stray satsuma rolls off the offering tray and lands square on a fly mid-buzz — <reading>さつ</reading>, flat, gone, before the enormous bell even finishes ringing. The shrine cats stare at the <reading>satsuma</reading> like it just committed a crime.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The one <radical>cow</radical> kept up at the <radical>Buddhist temple</radical> is never for eating, which makes it <kanji>special</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Brother <reading>Took</reading>, the temple monk, chants 「<reading>とく</reading>」 as he leads the one cow nobody may eat past the kitchen, because that cow is <kanji form="特">special</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Where <radical>each</radical> branch sits on the <radical>tree</radical> tells you its <kanji>status</kanji> without anybody saying a word.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every visitor who climbs the shrine's mossy steps and sees the cats ranked branch by branch just stops and <reading>gawks</reading>, throat catching on the same flat sound as the reading <reading>かく</reading>. The shrine's one enormous bell seems to echo it back once for every branch in the tree.

items.mnemonic_text: A roof over a pig (豕): the traditional house.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Any <radical>roof</radical> with a <radical>pig</radical> sprawled on its back under it is a <kanji>house</kanji>, since you only bring livestock indoors where you live.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading>, the fire-breathing crow, perches on the roof and croaks 「<reading>か</reading>」 down the chimney, warming the pig sprawled on its back inside the <kanji form="家">house</kanji>.
items.description: Beyond the building, 家 also means the household living in it, and as a suffix it marks an expert or professional rather than a house at all.

items.meaning_mnemonic: After enough <radical>sunrise</radical>s with nothing but dust underneath them, farmers <radical>beg</radical> for the end of the <kanji>drought</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The same heron kicks an empty tin <reading>can</reading> across the cracked mud out of pure boredom. It rolls to a stop with a hollow <reading>かん</reading> — the only sound this drought-cracked riverbank makes all summer.

items.mnemonic_text: A twisted shape over the heart (心): a bad feeling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When something the size of <radical>Asia</radical> is parked on top of one small <radical>heart</radical>, the only word for how that feels is <kanji>bad</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: With a weight the size of Asia parked on his one small heart, the night clerk <reading>Aku</reading> can only croak 「<reading>あく</reading>」 and admit he feels <kanji form="悪">bad</kanji>.
items.description: In casual speech this word doubles as a quick 'my bad' apology, not a claim that something is evil. The first time someone says it right at you, they are saying sorry.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A messenger who can <radical>run</radical> faster than the <radical>warrior</radical> chasing him will <kanji>surpass</kanji> him inside a mile.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the summit, a hiker named <reading>Etsu</reading> collapses against the vending machine and groans <reading>えつ</reading> between gasps — the same groan echoes down the trail every time someone else finally surpasses that last ridge.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>crooked mouth</radical> retelling the story the whole length of the <radical>road</radical> is certain to <kanji>overdo</kanji> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa the fire-breathing crow watches from the power line above the flooded bank. One puff of flame would do, but she can't stop — she keeps cawing <reading>か</reading>, <reading>か</reading>, like someone stuck repeating <reading>kah</reading>, torching the same branch long after it's ash.

items.mnemonic_text: A road (辶) that splits away (韋): to differ.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every strip of <radical>tanned leather</radical> you <radical>advance</radical> past on the riverbank path is dyed a shade off from the last, so all of them <kanji>differ</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At that same riverbank, a dyer named <reading>Evie</reading> pulls the drying strips down two at a time and holds them up to the sun. The moment a pair does not match, she snaps out a sharp <reading>い</reading> and dunks one straight back in the river.
items.description: In everyday speech, the verb form of this kanji often means simply 'no, that's wrong,' not a neutral 'these differ.' Used to answer someone, it corrects them and can sound blunt.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Wrapping somebody in fine <radical>clothing</radical> to <radical>protect</radical> them from criticism is one way to <kanji>praise</kanji> them.
items.reading_mnemonic: The shrine's caretaker, nicknamed <reading>Whoa</reading> because it's the only thing she ever says, watches the bell hum with approval. She breathes out a satisfied <reading>ほう</reading>, her robe still settling.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Hold a match to it, the <radical>fire</radical> takes, and <radical>so it is</radical> settled that the whole thing will <kanji>burn</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The neighborhood kids call Grandma Kane <reading>Nan</reading>, and when the incense flares she comes flying out stamping sparks off the mossy steps, yelling the cat's name so fast it comes out <reading>ねん</reading>. Picture Nan hollering ねん at that cat, and the reading burns itself in.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Water</radical> has never once stopped to <radical>demand</radical> permission before making you <kanji>get wet</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi mops the puddle, muttering <reading>じゅ</reading>, じゅ — it sounds exactly like the first syllable of <reading>juice</reading>, which is unfortunately also what the floor smells like now.
items.description: This character mostly means plain physical wetness — rain, tears, sweat. The "make love" sense is idiomatic, from a fixed phrase for an intimate scene in film or drama. On its own as a verb, it almost always just means damp, not romance.

items.mnemonic_text: Evening (夕) plus divination: reading fortunes outside.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A tortoise doing <radical>divination</radical> in the fading <radical>evening</radical> light has to shuffle <kanji>outside</kanji> to catch the last of the sun on its cracked shell.
items.reading_mnemonic: Out behind Grandma Kane's shrine at dusk, a fortune-telling guy keeps flipping his tortoise shell for one more reading. Each blank answer drags a long <reading>がい</reading> out of him, the groan a worn-out <reading>guy</reading> makes when the cards say wait.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="由">wherefore</kanji> of a dark morning is usually a <radical form="丨">stick</radical> someone jammed down through the top of the <radical form="日">sun</radical> window to hold the blind shut.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Yu</reading> the window cleaner finds the jammed blind, points straight at <reading>you</reading> and says 「<reading>ゆ</reading>」, because you are the whole <kanji form="由">wherefore</kanji> of the dark room.

items.mnemonic_text: A nose pointing at oneself: 'me', self.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You get this one for free, because the <radical>self</radical> radical you already know and the <kanji>self</kanji> kanji are the exact same character.
items.reading_mnemonic: A genie drifts up from the offering box at Grandma Kane's shrine, and when you ask who he takes orders from, he points a finger straight at his own nose and says <reading>じ</reading>. It comes out like a flat <reading>Gee</reading>, the sound you make when the answer was always going to be yourself.
items.description: All three are a tall box with inner lines. 自 has a short slanted stroke on top and two inner lines, splitting it into three parts. 目, eye, has those same three parts but no stroke on top. 白, white, has the top stroke but only one inner line, so it splits into two.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At closing time, Koichi, one <radical>person</radical> behind the till, stops itemizing the shelf. Each rice ball is a little <radical>jewel</radical>, and he refuses to <radical>split</radical> them into portions. He sweeps every one into a basket: the till beeps once for the <kanji>whole</kanji> lot.
items.reading_mnemonic: The new cashier, <reading>Zen</reading>, doesn't do partial sales. He scans the whole basket in one motion, muttering 「<reading>ぜん</reading>」 under his breath every night — like a chant for clearing the entire shelf in one go.

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) already up over the ground (十): early.
items.meaning_mnemonic: It is still <kanji>early</kanji> when the <radical>sun</radical> has climbed only <radical>ten</radical> finger-widths above the hills.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Sew</reading> the tailor holds all ten fingers up against the hills, sees the sun has barely cleared them, and hums <reading>そう</reading> because it is still <kanji form="早">early</kanji>.
items.description: The one kanji covers 'early' in time and 'fast' in pace at once; context, not the character, tells you which sense a sentence means.

items.mnemonic_text: A box enclosing plotted lines: a diagram, a map.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You cannot <radical>mow</radical> a walled <radical>enclosure</radical> into a tidy striped pattern without a <radical>small</radical> <kanji>diagram</kanji> of it in your hand.
items.reading_mnemonic: A zookeeper named <reading>Zoo</reading> is so hopeless among the identical pens that she keeps the whole park's <kanji>diagram</kanji> inked on her arm and jabs it, going 「<reading>ず</reading>」, at every fork in the path.

items.mnemonic_text: A jewel (玉) enclosed by borders: a country.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>country</kanji> is nothing but an <radical>enclosure</radical> of walls built around the one <radical>jewel</radical> its people refuse to share.
items.reading_mnemonic: The guard <reading>Cook</reading> stands at the one gate in the walls around the jewel, and nobody enters the <kanji form="国">country</kanji> until he slams his stamp down and barks 「<reading>こく</reading>」.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One line dragged over flat <radical>ground</radical> is just a mark until an <radical>open box</radical> frames it, which is the entire <radical>reason</radical> it now reads as a deliberate <kanji>brush-stroke</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The painter <reading>Gar</reading> drags one line across the flat ground, frames it inside an open box, and grunts 「<reading>が</reading>」 to declare it a <kanji form="画">brush-stroke</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth (口) not yet (未) full: tasting a bit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A bite sitting in your <radical>mouth</radical>, chewed but <radical>not yet</radical> gone down, still holds every bit of its <kanji>taste</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Koichi's konbini a food blogger tries the free onigiri sample and holds the bite on her tongue, humming <reading>み</reading> as if singing <reading>me</reading>, me, only me. She refuses to swallow until she has named every flavour, so the taste just goes on and on while the till beeps.
items.description: Beyond literal taste, 味 carries the figurative flavour of a thing. It sits inside the common words for 'meaning' and for 'interest', where it points at what something is really like rather than how it tastes on the tongue.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> on the left; on the right <radical>two</radical> bars over <radical>ground</radical>, each on a <radical>stick</radical>, <radical>split</radical> into legs at the foot. A tray, lifted with both hands for somebody above to take: to <kanji>submit</kanji> a thing.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kyou is the offering-bearer who never lowers the tray. He walks the entire length of the hall with it over his head, announcing himself at every pillar — 「<reading>きょう</reading>」 — until somebody finally takes the weight off him.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>cave</radical> that a whole <radical>construction</radical> crew has finished digging out is, for all that effort, still just an <kanji>empty</kanji> hollow in the hill.
items.reading_mnemonic: Once the digging crew packs up, the pigeon <reading>Coo</reading> flies into the dug-out cave, and his proud 「<reading>くう</reading>」 echoes off walls left completely <kanji form="空">empty</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>month</radical> of wear, a maker's <radical>stamp</radical> and a <radical>right hand</radical> mending it is the life of one piece of <kanji>clothing</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: After a month of wear, the tailor <reading>Fook</reading> checks the maker's stamp, mends the seam with his right hand and mutters 「<reading>ふく</reading>」 at this sorry piece of <kanji form="服">clothing</kanji>.
items.description: 服 by itself almost always means clothing, as in everyday words for Western-style clothes or a uniform. The senses obey and admit only appear buried inside fixed multi-character compounds about submission or confession - standing alone, this character just means clothes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>roof</kanji> is nothing but a sagging <radical>body</radical> sprawled overhead, and you only notice it the moment you <radical>arrive</radical> under it out of the rain.
items.reading_mnemonic: You arrive dripping out of the rain and hear the carpenter <reading>Oak</reading> sprawled on the sagging <kanji form="屋">roof</kanji> above you, barking 「<reading>おく</reading>」 as he nails it back up.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>mask</radical> radical and the <kanji>mask</kanji> kanji are the same, and since a mask is only a face you can take off, the character also means the face or features behind it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Menzo the actor wears a <kanji>mask</kanji> for every role so that behind it he could be any of a hundred <reading>men</reading>, and he crows 「<reading>めん</reading>」 at anyone who claims to know which.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Words</radical> counted out in <radical>ten</radical>s before a single one gets spoken aloud is a <kanji>plot</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The schemer <reading>Kay</reading> counts every word of her <kanji form="計">plot</kanji> out in tens on her fingers, whispering 「<reading>けい</reading>」 at each ten, and still speaks none of them aloud.
items.description: 計 usually means measure, plan, or total in real vocabulary, not a scheme in the dramatic sense this mnemonic uses. Treat the plot here as the calculating, tallying edge of that broader meaning, not a literal conspiracy.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> who can <radical>renew</radical> anything for you without leaving the counter is selling pure <kanji>convenience</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ben</reading> behind the counter renews your passport, phone plan and library card without leaving his stool, stamping each with a cheery 「<reading>べん</reading>」 of pure <kanji form="便">convenience</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When the <radical>sun</radical> sits at the exact <radical>center</radical> of the sky, the water below throws back its clearest <kanji>reflect</kanji>ion.
items.reading_mnemonic: Startled by his own doubled face in the water, the fisherman yelps 「<reading>Ay</reading>」 — 「<reading>えい</reading>」. The river throws the sound straight back at him a beat later, flat and unbothered, same as it did with the light.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sun</radical> too far off to warm anything, with its own <radical>life</radical> still burning away, is a <kanji>star</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, the star student, is first to point at it, hand shooting up before anyone else's, and announces it in one crisp syllable — <reading>せい</reading> — like she is always first to <reading>say</reading> the answer. The sports field goes quiet, impressed despite itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Something is <kanji>true</kanji> only when all <radical>ten</radical> inspectors, each checking with the same steady <radical>tool</radical>, come back with the same answer.
items.reading_mnemonic: The chief inspector <reading>Shin</reading> waits until all ten inspectors and their tools give the same answer, then chimes <reading>しん</reading> and stamps it <kanji form="真">true</kanji>.
items.description: Besides 'true', this kanji often acts as a prefix meaning 'dead-' or 'exactly': dead centre, right in the middle, pure white. In that spot it means 'completely', not 'true'.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>claw</radical> kept on the <radical>left-side</radical> and every <radical>measure</radical> taken well in advance is what marks out a <kanji>leader</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On that same field, Sho the tiny stage magician claps his white gloves, and a dove bursts skyward as the crowd yells <reading>Show</reading>! That's <reading>しょう</reading>, his one trick, performed the same way every time.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Carrying one tight <radical>bundle</radical> instead of three loose armfuls is what makes the <radical>road</radical> <kanji>quick</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top, the vending machine's countdown beeps in a clipped rhythm: <reading>そく</reading>, <reading>soak</reading>, <reading>そく</reading>. By the time he skids to a stop, his socks are soaked clean through from the sprint.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 勉 as a sweatband wrung out mid-cram with sheer <radical>power</radical>, soaking the page underneath. In Koichi's konbini, a student camped by the onigiri shelf pulls an all-nighter, refusing to be <radical>exempt</radical>, wringing the band out again and again: pure <kanji>exertion</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk ringing up onigiri all night, <reading>Ben</reading>, groans the same sympathetic <reading>べん</reading> every time the sweatband hits the counter, cheering the cramming on until the beeping till finally goes quiet.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 部 as a squat filing cabinet: a <radical>stand</radical> strut over a slot like an open <radical>mouth</radical>, beside a little <radical>village</radical> of drawers. A clerk yanks the wrong drawer, gets buried in someone else's forms, and slams shut the one marked for his own <kanji>section</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A moth called <reading>Bu</reading> gets shut inside that same drawer overnight and beats its wings against the forms, the frantic drumming going <reading>ぶ</reading>, <reading>ぶ</reading>, <reading>ぶ</reading>, until dawn finally opens the drawer and lets it stagger free.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>vehicle</radical> parked on a <radical>cloud</radical> finds nothing to grip, so its wheels just <kanji>revolve</kanji> and it stays put.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ten the circus bear sprints on a rolling log, spinning it under his paws while he stays in one spot, and the ringmaster shouts 「<reading>てん</reading>」, a perfect <reading>ten</reading>, every time the log <kanji>revolve</kanji>s once more.

items.mnemonic_text: A bow (弓) reinforced with a hard shell (虽): strong.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Thread that an <radical>insect</radical> spun inside its <radical>cocoon</radical> is tougher than steel wire, so a <radical>bow</radical> strung with it comes out impossibly <kanji>strong</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Retired weightlifter <reading>Kyo</reading> heaves on the bow strung with cocoon silk, cannot even bend it, and grunts 「<reading>きょう</reading>」 at a string this <kanji form="強">strong</kanji>.
items.description: After a quantity, this kanji reads 'and a bit more' rather than 'strong'. An amount with it on the end sits just over the round number, not far above it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>dog</radical> roasting over a <radical>fire</radical> under a full <radical>moon</radical> is the <kanji>sort of thing</kanji> that needs explaining.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk, whom regulars just call <reading>Zen</reading> for his permanent shrug, mutters a flat <reading>ぜん</reading> every time someone asks for specifics, sliding the mystery onigiri back onto the shelf without another word. Say his name fast enough and it collapses into the same flat <reading>ぜん</reading> — shrug included.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Getting your <radical>hand</radical> up at the <radical>right</radical> moment is the whole skill of knowing how to <kanji>propose</kanji> something.
items.reading_mnemonic: Tei, a deer too formal for the konbini, holds an empty tray at arm's length over that same counter like he's presenting a proposal, and repeats <reading>てい</reading>, <reading>tray</reading>, until someone puts something on it. Nobody ever does; he holds the pose anyway.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Pull the <radical form="冖">cover</radical> up one <radical form="夕">evening</radical> under a <radical form="罒">net</radical> woven from <radical form="艹">grass</radical>, and it catches every bad thought so only a good <kanji form="夢">dream</kanji> slips through.
items.reading_mnemonic: A cow called <reading>Moo</reading> chews through the catcher above your bed in the night, so now every <kanji form="夢">dream</kanji> you have ends with a huge 「<reading>む</reading>」.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Any <kanji>building</kanji> is just an empty shell until a <radical>bureaucrat</radical> moves in with his stamp and there is enough <radical>food (left)</radical> over from lunch to keep him at the desk.
items.reading_mnemonic: The night caretaker <reading>Khan</reading> clears the bureaucrat's leftover lunch off the desk and snaps 「<reading>かん</reading>」 at anyone still stamping papers in his <kanji form="館">building</kanji> after closing.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="大">big</radical> bowl of <radical form="米">rice</radical> looks all the same until you press your <radical form="頁">head</radical> right down to it and see that every grain is a different <kanji form="類">sort</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Louie</reading> the fussy chef peers into that bowl, runs out of names for each new <kanji form="類">sort</kanji> of grain, and labels them all 「<reading>るい</reading>」 after himself.

items.mnemonic_text: A flexed arm pushing: power and strength.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>power</radical> radical and the <kanji>power</kanji> kanji are the same character, and strength is just that same power once you can feel it straining in your muscles.
items.reading_mnemonic: The weightlifter <reading>Rocky</reading> bends one arm at the elbow until the muscle bulges hard as a rock, and grunts 「<reading>りょく</reading>」 at all that <kanji form="力">power</kanji>.
items.description: The one to watch is 九, 'nine'. In 力 the long stroke drops straight down the right side and ends in a small hook curling to the left. In 九 that stroke swings out wide to the right and finishes with a hook low on the right, and its first stroke pokes out past the top-left corner.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> folded neatly into a <radical>wide box</radical> is very definitely <kanji>inside</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi flings the fridge door open and the man just shivers, chin on his knees, repeating one flat syllable: <reading>ない</reading>. It's the same sound the staff now call him by, <reading>Nye</reading> — the third time this month he's pulled the same fridge stunt.

items.mnemonic_text: A person with sparks flying off each side: fire.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You already know the <radical>fire</radical> radical, and the <kanji>fire</kanji> kanji is that same upright log with sparks flicking off both sides.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa, the fire-breathing crow, lands on the upright log and gives one <reading>caw</reading>, and her 「<reading>か</reading>」 spits two sparks off its sides and sets the log on <kanji form="火">fire</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One stroke <radical>slides</radical> down from the top left across a bar of <radical>ground</radical>, met by a <radical>right hand</radical> rising underneath. Two hands close on each other, nobody paid, nobody in charge: that is a <kanji>friend</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Yuu is always there before you, hand already out. He draws the greeting into a long two-beat call across the car park — 「<reading>ゆう</reading>」 — before you have shut the car door. ゆう means somebody is glad to see you.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Put your own <radical>power</radical> behind one more <radical>mouth</radical> and you <kanji>add</kanji> real weight to the argument.
items.reading_mnemonic: Outside on the power line, <reading>Kaa</reading> watches the tower climb, and every new onigiri triggers a tiny puff of flame and a screech of <reading>か</reading>. By the tenth <reading>か</reading> the crow finally overheats and topples the whole stack just to make the counting stop.

items.mnemonic_text: A lamp's flame steady atop its stand: the main, central one.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Screw a <radical>lid</radical> down over the <radical>king</radical>'s crown and you seal in the one <kanji>lord</kanji> whose word the whole house has to follow.
items.reading_mnemonic: Footman <reading>Shoe</reading> screws the lid down over the king's crown with a crisp 「<reading>しゅ</reading>」, sealing in the one <kanji form="主">lord</kanji> whose word the whole house must follow.
items.description: Under its top dot, this is exactly 王 'king / jewel': three bars crossed by a standing post. 王 has nothing above its top bar; 主 adds one short dot there. Lose that dot and you have written king, not lord.

items.mnemonic_text: In the evening (夕) you call out a mouth's (口) name.
items.meaning_mnemonic: In the <radical>evening</radical> nobody can see your face, so your <radical>mouth</radical> has to give your <kanji>name</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: In the dark evening nobody can see <reading>May</reading>'s face, so her mouth calls 「<reading>めい</reading>」 out into the night to tell everyone her <kanji form="名">name</kanji>.
items.description: 名 and 多 both start with the same slanted three-stroke piece. 名 finishes with a small closed box beneath it. 多 repeats that slanted piece a second time instead, so it is one shape stacked twice.

items.mnemonic_text: A dangling shape on the side of the head: an ear.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Good news for once, the <radical>ear</radical> radical you already know and the <kanji>ear</kanji> kanji are the very same character.
items.reading_mnemonic: A gnat buzzes into the folds of the tall rim on the side of your head, and you yelp a startled <reading>gee</reading>, 「<reading>じ</reading>」, slapping your own <kanji form="耳">ear</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Taking a <radical>knife</radical> to your own <radical>grain</radical> and selling the better half of it is <kanji>profit</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same konbini scale, the clerk tucks a dry <reading>reed</reading> behind his ear for luck. Every time a sack outweighs itself, he snaps the reed and grins, muttering a stretched <reading>り</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Turn round and take the <radical>opposite</radical> <radical>road</radical> back the way you came to <kanji>return</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: That startled hen at the summit vending machine won't shut up about it. Every time the boomerang whips past, she screeches <reading>へん</reading>, like a slapstick chicken shouting <reading>hen</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: Grass on top of a person changing (化): a blooming flower.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When ordinary <radical>grass</radical> gets tired of being green and <radical>change</radical>s its top into colour, what stands there is a <kanji>flower</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa, the fire-breathing crow, lets out a <reading>caw</reading> over the green grass, and her hot 「<reading>か</reading>」 scorches each blade's tip into red and gold until it stands as a <kanji form="花">flower</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Whoever controls the <radical>water</radical> gets the <radical>pedestal</radical>, and from up there they <kanji>reign</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The stone-stacker, a quiet type the other kids call <reading>Ji</reading> because he never says more than one syllable, watches his pool go still and finally speaks: <reading>じ</reading>, and nothing else, satisfied.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Being handed <radical>three</radical> <radical>big</radical> silk <radical>cocoon</radical>s with no explanation at all leaves anybody <kanji>nonplussed</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The bell's still ringing when the <reading>sun</reading> clears the shrine roof and floods the steps with light. The cat squints up at it, hisses one flat <reading>さん</reading>, and doesn't move an inch.
items.description: 参 splits between two senses. As the humble verb 参る it means to go or come. On its own or in compounds it instead carries nonplussed, worn out, at your wit's end. The shape doesn't distinguish them; only the sentence does.

items.mnemonic_text: Wings spread mid-motion: to fly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>fly</radical> radical and the <kanji>fly</kanji> kanji are the same character, a point you earn just by knowing your radicals.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Hina</reading> the chick lifts her head and beats both wings hard, wheezing a thin 「<reading>ひ</reading>」 with every flap until she can finally <kanji form="飛">fly</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A roof (宀) reaching (至) to enclose a room.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>room</kanji> is the patch of floor under a <radical>roof</radical> where your journey finally <radical>arrive</radical>s and you drop your bags.
items.reading_mnemonic: The moment your bags hit the floor, the maid <reading>Sheets</reading> arrives with fresh linen, muttering 「<reading>しつ</reading>」 as she makes up the <kanji form="室">room</kanji> under your new roof.
items.description: 室 is the formal 'room' in names for purpose-built rooms, not the everyday word for a room at home.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>sound</kanji> is anything that makes you <radical>stand</radical> straight up, alert, in the middle of an otherwise silent <radical>day</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Owen stands straight up at every <kanji form="音">sound</kanji> that breaks the silent day, sure it is his to <reading>own</reading>, and seals it in a jar marked <reading>おん</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: Bones (歹) left over after the cut (戔): what remains.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Dig a grave too <radical>shallow</radical> after a stroke of <radical>bad luck</radical> and part of what you buried will always <kanji>remain</kanji> poking up out of the dirt.
items.reading_mnemonic: A gravedigger named <reading>Zan</reading> groans 「<reading>ざん</reading>」 over the shallow grave, because however much dirt he shovels on, one boot will <kanji form="残">remain</kanji> poking out.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Sitting down to <radical>relax</radical> under a <radical>tree</radical> is where every decent <kanji>plan</kanji> actually gets made.
items.reading_mnemonic: Anzu, a trail scout who reaches the mountain-top desk every dawn, unfolds the scrawled plan with a huge <reading>yawn</reading>. She mutters <reading>あん</reading> under her breath, checking the route while the vending machine hums beside her.

items.mnemonic_text: Feathers (羽) over white (白): a bird practicing to fly, to learn.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>learn</kanji> a skill the way down becomes flight, by beating each <radical>white</radical> tuft over and over until it stiffens into a real <radical>feather</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fledgling named <reading>Shoe</reading> beats each white tuft over and over, puffing 「<reading>しゅう</reading>」 with every stroke, until the down stiffens into a real feather, which is how you <kanji form="習">learn</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Turning plain <radical>millet</radical> into something worth <radical>going</radical> across town for is an <kanji>art</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A boy at the edge of the field is nicknamed <reading>Juts</reading> for the way his chin juts out. When that seventh plate finally lands, he shouts <reading>じゅつ</reading> so loud his chin juts out even further.

items.mnemonic_text: Thread (糸) running straight through the loom (圣): to pass through time.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <radical>thread</radical> strung through a monk's <radical>holy</radical> prayer beads has to <kanji>pass through</kanji> all one hundred and eight of them without ever snapping.
items.reading_mnemonic: The monk's novice <reading>Kay</reading> strings the prayer beads by lamplight, sighing 「<reading>けい</reading>」 each time the thread must <kanji form="経">pass through</kanji> one more of the hundred and eight.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>heart</radical> that goes <radical>blue-green</radical> every time she walks past is doing nothing to hide its <kanji>feelings</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: An old pilgrim named <reading>Joe</reading> climbs to Grandma Kane's shrine every week and presses his palm flat to the weeping bell. He lets out the same low groan before the sob catches him: <reading>じょう</reading>. The cats have learned to flinch right on cue.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> handed a <radical>sweeper</radical> the moment she walks in is being called a <kanji>lady</kanji> to her face.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the shrine gate, Fumi leans her broom against the rail and blows out a long <reading>phew</reading> — a breathy 「<reading>ふ</reading>」 that scatters the incense smoke. Then she picks the broom up to finish the steps.

items.mnemonic_text: A workbench stacked with tools: one's trade, business.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Turning the stiff <radical>bristles</radical> you comb off a <radical>sheep</radical> into hairbrushes nailed to a <radical>tree</radical>-stump counter is a strange little <kanji>business</kanji> that somehow pays.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi liked those sheep-bristle hairbrushes so much he now sells them right by the onigiri shelf, his first real side business. The barcode scanner he calls <reading>Gyo</reading> screeches <reading>ぎょう</reading> each time a brush slides past the beeping till.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>All</radical> of the <radical>heart</radical> arriving at once and none of the head arriving at all is <kanji>emotion</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: When all of her heart arrives at once and none of her head does, <reading>Khan</reading> can only gasp 「<reading>かん</reading>」, swamped by raw <kanji form="感">emotion</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>long kimono</radical> dragging down a <radical>road</radical> with no end to it makes anywhere look <kanji>distant</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On that same endless road, a hiker named <reading>Enzo</reading> collapses face down at the mile marker, wheezing the sound <reading>えん</reading> into the gravel. He swears the horizon moved again while he blinked.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Let the same thing <radical>pierce</radical> your <radical>heart</radical> often enough and you will get <kanji>accustomed</kanji> to it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Behind the counter, Koichi restocks the drink case so many times his hand does it alone — each can lands with a flat clink that sounds like <reading>かん</reading>, someone saying <reading>khan</reading> without the h. He's stopped hearing it. That's how accustomed he's become.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>tree</radical> frame and <radical>how many</radical> threads you can be bothered to count is the whole of a <kanji>loom</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki, the tree spirit living in the riverbank's hollow trunk, blows through the abandoned loom every time the wind gusts, rattling its threads. She giggles <reading>き</reading>, <reading>き</reading>, a sound like a rusty <reading>key</reading> turning, and the shuttle clacks on by itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Words</radical> you <radical>shoot</radical> off before thinking are exactly the ones you have to <kanji>apologize</kanji> for later.
items.reading_mnemonic: The archer at the riverbank, a title everyone shortens to <reading>Shah</reading>, still cannot fire a straight shot. Every arrow that misses gets the same muttered <reading>しゃ</reading>, half apology, half excuse, as he bows and fishes it out of the reeds.
items.description: This kanji covers more than sorry: the same character also carries formal thanks and, in some compounds, an outright refusal or decline. Underneath all three is one idea, a formal spoken response rather than plain regret, so context decides whether it reads as apology, gratitude, or a firm no.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="議">deliberation</kanji> is a room full of people spending their <radical form="言">words</radical> back and forth until the calm, fair choice of <radical form="義">righteousness</radical> finally wins.
items.reading_mnemonic: A goose named <reading>Gee</reading> sits in on every <kanji form="議">deliberation</kanji>, honking 「<reading>ぎ</reading>」 over each speaker until the whole room gives up and votes his way.

items.mnemonic_text: Three peaks rising up: a mountain range.
items.meaning_mnemonic: This one is a freebie, since the <radical>mountain</radical> radical and the <kanji>mountain</kanji> kanji are the exact same character.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker slogs up the steep mountain trail toward the lone vending machine at the top. Right as she reaches the summit the <reading>sun</reading> clears the ridge and blinds her, and all she can manage is <reading>さん</reading> before feeding in her coins.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>cow</radical> radical you already know and the <kanji>cow</kanji> kanji are the exact same character, so this one is a free point for learning your radicals.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Gyoo</reading> the milkmaid grabs the <kanji form="牛">cow</kanji> by its one slanted horn and hugs its broad shoulders so hard that it wheezes 「<reading>ぎゅう</reading>」.

items.mnemonic_text: A stylized heart shape with three drips of feeling.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>heart</radical> radical and the <kanji>heart</kanji> kanji are one and the same, and because old Japanese placed thought in the chest rather than the head, the shape also means mind.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Shin</reading> the jogger runs so hard that his cartoon <kanji form="心">heart</kanji> pops out three beating dots, and he gasps 「<reading>しん</reading>」 as each one lands on his sore shin.
items.description: The one to watch is 必 (necessary). Both have the same curved, swooping base and a scatter of short dots, but 必 drives a straight diagonal stroke right through the center of the shape, running down toward the lower left. 心 has nothing crossing it: just the open curved base and three separate dots resting around it. If a line spears through the middle, you are looking at 必, not 心.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Jam a soft silk <radical form="厶">cocoon</radical> into a leaking pipe and twist it with <radical form="廾">two hands</radical> to let the water through or hold it back, and you have built a <kanji form="弁">valve</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ben</reading> the plumber bends over the dripping pipe all day, grunting 「<reading>べん</reading>」 each time he twists his soft little <kanji form="弁">valve</kanji> shut, and it squeaks back open the moment he stands up.

items.mnemonic_text: A person standing on the ground line: to stand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>stand</radical> radical and the <kanji>stand</kanji> kanji are the very same shape and sense, so this one costs you nothing new.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the sports field the coach at Sei's school makes the whole class stand at attention until someone tips over. You outlast everyone, but your saluting <reading>wrist</reading> locks up stiff, and each hot throb of it beats out <reading>りつ</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When your <radical form="扌">hand</radical> has to pull the coins out of the silk <radical form="厶">cocoon</radical> where you keep them hidden, it is time to <kanji form="払">pay</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The miser <reading>Foots</reading> will only <kanji form="払">pay</kanji> with his feet, so he kicks each coin out of its hiding place and across the counter, muttering 「<reading>ふつ</reading>」 with every kick.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Put a <radical>lid</radical> on the argument and send your <radical>father</radical> out to <kanji>mingle</kanji> with the guests instead.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi doesn't even blink. He steps clean over the tangled pile, scanner beeping, muttering <reading>こう</reading>, <reading>こう</reading>, <reading>こう</reading> like a checkout jingle, a steady <reading>coo coo coo</reading>, restocking the shelf before the mingled mob has even worked itself loose.

items.meaning_mnemonic: If you <radical form="𠂊">crouch</radical> in the very spot where the <radical form="厄">unlucky</radical> man got hit by a falling rock, you are doing something <kanji form="危">dangerous</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> the tree spirit squeaks 「<reading>き</reading>！」 from her old pine above the falling rocks to warn you the spot is <kanji form="危">dangerous</kanji>, then giggles when you duck one second too late.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (人) leaning on a tree (木): resting.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the mountain trail, you spot a <radical>person</radical> slumped sideways against a <radical>tree</radical>, leaning into the trunk like it's the comfiest chair in the world. A <radical>person</radical> plus the tree they're propped against — that's someone taking a well-earned <kanji>rest</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker leaning on that tree lets out a huge, happy sigh — "<reading>きゅう</reading>!" — the sound of every muscle finally letting go. Every time you picture that person melting into rest, you hear that きゅう escape.
items.description: Means "rest" and shows up in everyday words for taking breaks and days off, like 休み.
