items.meaning_mnemonic: A man slumped in a waiting-room chair with a huge <radical form="欠">yawn</radical> keeps missing his turn, until two chips of <radical form="冫">ice</radical> down his shirt make him jump up just as the clerk calls <kanji form="次">next</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk <reading>Gee</reading> never bothers to say <kanji form="次">next</kanji> in full, so she just barks 「<reading>じ</reading>！」 across the waiting room, and the dripping man in the front chair jumps every single time.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>body</radical> that answers every <radical>phrase</radical> you say with another form to fill in is working in a <kanji>bureau</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Wedged into that same booth, a customer three forms deep chokes on chalky bureau dust drifting off the tax stacks, coughing out something between a wheeze and <reading>きょく</reading>. Koichi just nods, because everyone who reaches window three sounds exactly like they're trying to say <reading>choke</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the riverbank, the water freezes over so fast that a dragonfly gets sealed inside the <radical>ice</radical>, wings still spread. Beside it, a <radical>person</radical>'s single bootprint is <radical>stamp</radical>ed into the same frozen crust. The whole surface holds that <radical>one</radical> frozen, glassy chill: <kanji>cool</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A swimmer named <reading>Ray</reading> wades into the river and the cold hits so fast he gasps <reading>れい</reading> — like shouting his own name — freezing mid-step right where the dragonfly sits trapped in the ice.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Whatever hangs at the top of a <radical form="木">tree</radical>, round and split into four green squares like a tiny <radical form="田">rice field</radical>, is its <kanji form="果">fruit</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading> the fire-breathing crow lands on the top branch, roasts the ripest <kanji form="果">fruit</kanji> with one puff of flame, and caws 「<reading>か</reading>！」 because now it is far too hot to eat.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="日">sun</radical>ny day with not one sign anywhere telling you do <radical form="勿">not</radical> is as <kanji form="易">easy</kanji> as a day can get, because nothing you try is against the rules.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Eckie</reading> the lizard naps on top of the empty sign post all afternoon, sighing 「<reading>えき</reading>」, since a sunny day with nothing to obey is <kanji form="易">easy</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>walk</kanji> is slow travel where your feet <radical>stop</radical> flat on the ground so often that you cover only a <radical>few</radical> steps a minute.
items.reading_mnemonic: On the steep mountain trail, Grandma Kane climbs one slow step at a time, leaning her full weight on an old garden <reading>hoe</reading> and grunting <reading>ほ</reading> each time a foot lands flat. At this rate the vending machine at the top is an hour off, but she plants the hoe and takes the next step anyway.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Split a <radical>tree</radical> and the <radical>opposite</radical> face of that cut comes away as one flat <kanji>plank</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream at the same crossing, the chef <reading>Han</reading> — the one who serves every dish split exactly in half — squats over the cracked plank and slices his lunch on it. He mutters 「<reading>はん</reading>」 with each cut: half for him, half for the current.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Every grain of <kanji form="砂">sand</kanji> is a <radical form="石">stone</radical> that the waves wore down until only a <radical form="少">few</radical> crumbs of it were left.
items.reading_mnemonic: A mason who tries to <reading>saw</reading> a boulder in half ends up knee-deep in <kanji form="砂">sand</kanji>, spitting 「<reading>さ</reading>」 every time the grit gets between his teeth.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Every</radical> river's <radical>water</radical> ends up in the same place eventually, and that place is the <kanji>sea</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A river guide named <reading>Kai</reading> rides every river's water down to the place it all ends, shouting 「<reading>かい</reading>」 as the current spits him out into the open <kanji form="海">sea</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Counting <radical>twenty</radical> paces out from the <radical>shelter</radical> with your <radical>right hand</radical> raised measures the <kanji>degrees</kanji> of the slope.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker called <reading>Doe</reading> paces twenty steps out from the shelter, right hand raised, and stamps a flat 「<reading>ど</reading>」 on each one to measure the <kanji form="度">degrees</kanji> of the slope.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Ranking every soldier by the length of the <radical>pike</radical> he can carry gives you a rough <kanji>grade</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The stonemason, a squat old man everyone on the trail calls <reading>Dan</reading>, stamps your hiking permit. He grunts 「<reading>だん</reading>」 once for every stair he's decided you're worthy of, then turns his back.

items.mnemonic_text: A tree (木) crossed with mingling students: a school.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Plant a <radical>tree</radical> along each path so hundreds of kids <radical>mingle</radical> in the shade where the walkways cross, and you have built a <kanji>school</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi the konbini king becomes the <kanji form="校">school</kanji> <reading>coach</reading>, blowing his whistle under the tree where the paths cross and barking 「<reading>こう</reading>」 at the kids who mingle in its shade.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The open ground between the <radical>shelter</radical> and the <radical>courts</radical> is the <kanji>courtyard</kanji> everybody has to cross.
items.reading_mnemonic: The groundskeeper, named <reading>Tei</reading>, sprints after the goat squatting in the courtyard, tripping over the raked gravel and yelling <reading>てい</reading>, <reading>てい</reading> with every failed lunge, gravel spraying across the whole swept quiet.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Splash <radical form="氵">water</radical> on a campfire to <kanji form="消">extinguish</kanji> it, and all that is left is a thin gray <radical form="肖">resemblance</radical> of the fire drawn in smoke.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Sho</reading> the tiny magician ends every <reading>show</reading> by tipping a teacup of water over his candle to <kanji form="消">extinguish</kanji> it, squeaking 「<reading>しょう</reading>」 while his doves cough in the smoke.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Land the <radical>village</radical> claimed <radical>beforehand</radical> and then never got round to fencing is still open <kanji>plains</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The village never fenced the land it claimed beforehand, so a herder gallops across the open <kanji form="野">plains</kanji> yelling <reading>yah</reading>, 「<reading>や</reading>」, where the posts should be.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>vegetable</kanji> is the one leafy plant you <radical>pick</radical> out of a whole patch of <radical>grass</radical> and actually agree to eat.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Sigh</reading> the grump picks the one leafy <kanji form="菜">vegetable</kanji> out of the whole patch of grass and lets out a long, defeated 「<reading>さい</reading>」 at having to eat it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="王">king</radical> who trusts only what he can <radical form="見">see</radical> right in front of his face cares about nothing but the <kanji form="現">present</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At roll call, <reading>Gen</reading> the palace guard shouts 「<reading>げん</reading>」 one inch from the throne, because anyone out of the ruler's sight is not counted as <kanji form="現">present</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Stacking <radical>all</radical> the rooms up a <radical>hill</radical> instead of spreading them out is how you get another <kanji>storey</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A monk named <reading>Kai</reading> climbs the shrine steps every morning, counting each landing aloud so he doesn't lose track: <reading>かい</reading>, one floor, <reading>かい</reading>, another. The cats sunning themselves on the steps stop washing just to watch him pass.
items.description: 階 rarely stands alone as the everyday word for a storey. In practice it almost always attaches to a number as the counter for building floors. きざはし is a rare, literary reading for a staircase; かい is the reading actually used day to day.

items.meaning_mnemonic: To stop a <radical form="吉">good luck</radical> wish from flying away, you <kanji form="結">tie</kanji> it down with a tight knot of <radical form="糸">thread</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Visitors <kanji form="結">tie</kanji> so many paper wishes to the horns of <reading>Ketsy</reading> the shrine goat that she bleats 「<reading>けつ</reading>」 every time a knot is pulled tight.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Holding a <radical form="叚">false</radical> face up to your boss lets you slip outside into the <radical form="日">sun</radical>, and every hour you steal that way is <kanji form="暇">spare time</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading> the fire-breathing crow has so much <kanji form="暇">spare time</kanji> on his sunny power line that he spots your mask, burns a hole in it, and caws 「<reading>か</reading>」 until your boss looks up.

items.mnemonic_text: Speech (言) with a mouth counting to five (五): words and language.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A waterfall of <radical>speech</radical> pours down into a waiting <radical>mouth</radical> below. The mouth swallows every word whole without chewing once. Stuffed with so many words, it finally speaks a whole <kanji>language</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A chatty man named <reading>Go</reading> stands under the waterfall of speech with his mouth wide open, gulping 「<reading>ご</reading>」 after every word until he can speak a whole <kanji form="語">language</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A slash over ten (十) multiplies it into a thousand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Drop a single <radical>slash</radical> across your tally of <radical>ten</radical> and the whole count suddenly jumps to a <kanji>thousand</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at that smeared tally wall in the school hallway, Sei counts the marks, gives up, and decides to just <reading>send</reading> the whole impossible number through as one lump sum. It goes as <reading>せん</reading>, a flat thousand that nobody is ever going to recount.
items.description: 千 opens with a slash from the upper right, above one horizontal and the upright. 十 (ten) is that shape without the slash. 午 (noon) keeps the slash but runs two horizontals. 干 (dry or shield) has two horizontals as well, but a flat straight top instead of a slash.

items.mnemonic_text: A single hooked mark standing for a whole ten thousand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>ten thousand</radical> radical and the <kanji>ten thousand</kanji> kanji are the same, so this is one review you get for nothing.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Manny</reading> the deli clerk chases the ticket rolling from the machine down to the floor, reads the number on it, and sighs 「<reading>まん</reading>」, because it says <kanji form="万">ten thousand</kanji>.
items.description: The look-alike 方 (direction / person) puts a short slanted stroke above its first horizontal line; 'ten thousand' has no stroke there. Its last stroke also drops in a near-straight squarish leg, where 'ten thousand' swings that stroke out in one wide sweep.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>evening</radical> radical you already learned and the <kanji>evening</kanji> kanji are the same character, so knowing your radicals cold just handed you this one for free.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Seki</reading> the shrine sweeper waits for the thin crescent moon to slip out from behind its small cloud, then calls 「<reading>せき</reading>」, because that moon means <kanji form="夕">evening</kanji> has come.

items.mnemonic_text: A cross pushed into the ground: earth and soil.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You met this shape already as the <radical>earth</radical> radical, and the <kanji>earth</kanji> kanji is the very same character, used just as happily for the loose soil that earth breaks down into.
items.reading_mnemonic: A gardener hammers the wooden signpost into the flat ground with a deep 「<reading>ど</reading>」, and the soft <kanji form="土">earth</kanji> squishes up around it like <reading>dough</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: Big (大) with an extra drop of size: thick, fat.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One extra <radical>drop</radical> of fat on someone already stretched as <radical>big</radical> as they can stand is all it takes to turn big into <kanji>fat</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The man is already as big as he can stand, so one extra drop of fat makes his <reading>tie</reading> snap 「<reading>たい</reading>」 off a neck now too <kanji form="太">fat</kanji> for it.
items.description: 太 is 大 'big' with a single dot added low, tucked into the fork between the legs. Plain 大 has no dot at all. In 犬 'dog' the dot sits high, up at the top-right corner, not down in the fork.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>generation</radical> radical and the <kanji>generation</kanji> kanji are the same, and since the people of one generation are the people of one world, it also means world or society.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei, the star student, steps onto the long bar beside grandparent, parent and child to have her <reading>say</reading>: a smug 「<reading>せい</reading>」 that her <kanji form="世">generation</kanji> is the best post in the row.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>stick</radical> raised up into the <radical>sun</radical> is the old signal that you <kanji>have the honor to</kanji> speak next.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shin catches the arrow's fletching on his <reading>shin</reading> as it flies past the same target, yelps <reading>しん</reading>, and doubles over clutching his shin — still bowing out of habit as he hops on one foot.
items.description: 申 covers three unrelated uses. As 申す, humble language for say, it gives have the honor to. On its own it also names the monkey sign of the zodiac, and the old two-hour block from 3 to 5PM. Only context tells you which sense you're reading.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A mound of <radical>earth</radical> sits on top, underneath a sealed <radical>cocoon</radical> tucked out of sight. Whatever was inside wrapped up and went under the soil. Dig the mound over: nothing is left. It is <kanji>gone</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kyo is the magician who buries things and cannot get them back. He taps the mound, says 「<reading>きょ</reading>」 with a flourish, and that is genuinely the end of the trick. No reappearance, no second half. きょ, and it is gone.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Look at the <radical>tree</radical>: a <radical>stick</radical> straight up, branches <radical>split</radical> aside. A <radical>lid</radical> stroke lies atop, longer than the <radical>one</radical> below — the twig's last inch: the <kanji>end</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Matsu is the woodsman who only ever takes the tip. He climbs the whole tree, snips the last bud off the top of it, and calls down 「<reading>まつ</reading>」 to say he has got there. まつ means there is nothing above him.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Crouch</radical> behind a <radical>halberd</radical> for long enough and you <kanji>turn into</kanji> a soldier whether you meant to or not.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei reaches the summit first, hand up before anyone can ask, and plants herself by the vending machine that just turned into a bench. She declares it like a quiz answer: a crisp, smug <reading>せい</reading>, and hikers who arrive late swear they can still hear that <reading>say</reading> echo off the rocks.

items.mnemonic_text: One (一) over a white (白) sheet counted a hundred times.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>one</radical> stroke sits on top of a blinding <radical>white</radical> light bulb. The light is so bright the stroke multiplies into copies of itself. Soon there are exactly a <kanji>hundred</kanji> strokes glowing on the ceiling.
items.reading_mnemonic: Staring into the blinding white bulb gives you a <reading>hiccup</reading>, and each 「<reading>ひゃく</reading>」 copies the stroke on top until a <kanji form="百">hundred</kanji> of them glow on the ceiling.
items.description: 百 is 白 with one extra stroke on top. 白 caps its box with a small flick; 百 turns that cap into a full-width horizontal bar.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>official</radical> whose <radical>mouth</radical> is always hanging open to bark one more order is exactly the man everyone is forced to call <kanji>mister</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: That same barking official trudges up the mossy steps of Grandma Kane's shrine. The cats swarm him and web him into a fat silk <reading>cocoon</reading> in seconds, and every command he keeps shouting from inside now comes out as a muffled <reading>くん</reading>.
items.description: Not a polite title. As a name-suffix it marks a junior, a classmate, or a young man rather than a superior. As a stand-alone word it is a familiar 'you' that can sound blunt with someone you barely know.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Knowing where the <radical>water</radical> has already <radical>gone</radical> before you start digging is what having a <kanji>method</kanji> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hou, an owl who lives on the flume post, keeps watch for cheaters. Whenever a drop tries to leap the channel early, he swivels his head and hoots <reading>ほう</reading> — a low <reading>whoa</reading> that echoes off the water — until the drop falls back into line.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Once the last <radical>person</radical> outdoors presses a <radical>lid</radical> down over the fading <radical>evening</radical>, not one <radical>drop</radical> of light escapes, and the sealed black that follows is <kanji>night</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The last guard outdoors, <reading>Yah</reading>, presses the lid down over the fading evening with a grunted 「<reading>や</reading>」, and not one drop of light escapes the <kanji form="夜">night</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) not yet (未) grown: the younger sister.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> who is <radical>not yet</radical> old enough for anyone to call her one is the <kanji>younger sister</kanji> of the house.
items.reading_mnemonic: Not yet old enough to be called a woman, the <kanji form="妹">younger sister</kanji> of the house clutches every toy and squeals <reading>my</reading>, 「<reading>まい</reading>」, at anyone who reaches for it.
items.description: The look-alike is 姉, 'older sister'. Both share the 'woman' element on the left, so the difference is all on the right. 妹 has 'not yet': a tree with two crossbars, the upper shorter, and two short diagonals flaring out at the foot like roots. 姉 instead has a small tick atop a boxy cloth shape, with one long vertical dropping straight through and out the bottom, and no flaring feet.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> sweeps her yard with a <radical>broom</radical> tied to a <radical>stick</radical>. She works until the bare <radical>ground</radical> is spotless. The neighbors call her the tidy <kanji>wife</kanji> of the house.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sai is the one who actually decides. Ask her husband anything and he glances sideways at her first; she gives one flat 「<reading>さい</reading>」 and that is the answer on behalf of both of them. さい settles it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Deciding what is <radical>correct</radical> and then taking <radical>action</radical> on it in front of everybody is the whole of <kanji>politics</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sei doesn't stop at the flagpole. She marches the whole class into rows and claps them straight. Every clap lands on the same syllable, sharp as a ruler on a desk: 「<reading>せい</reading>」 — the way you'd <reading>say</reading> a drill sergeant's count.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>cult</radical> and your <radical>elder brother</radical> finally agreeing on something is reason enough to <kanji>celebrate</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The coach gets <reading>shook</reading> so hard by the shoulder-ride that his whistle flies into the bleachers. <reading>しゅく</reading>! <reading>しゅく</reading>! the players chant with every shake — and a second later, he tips backward into the equipment cart.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Stopping</radical> halfway down the <radical>road</radical> and walking back the way you came is a <kanji>retreat</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker is nicknamed <reading>Ty</reading>, and halfway down his retreat he catches a bootlace and yelps <reading>たい</reading>, sliding the last few steps on his backside past the vending machine he never got to try.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> stands in the field, thin at the very top. Someone plucks the <radical>small</radical> piece from its tip. That tiny sliver of time becomes one <kanji>second</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Byou is the hospital timekeeper with the stopwatch, and she counts out loud in a flat clipped bark — 「<reading>びょう</reading>」, びょう, びょう — one for every tick. She will not speed up and she will not stop. びょう is a single second landing.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You jab a finger at your own <radical>self</radical> to answer for something. Your <radical>heart</radical> pounds beneath it, working overtime from the shock. What rushes between the two, in and out, is your <kanji>breath</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Soku is the swimmer who comes up after far too long under and takes one enormous ragged gulp — 「<reading>そく</reading>」 — nose first, heart going like a hammer. That is what a breath you badly needed sounds like. そく.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A young <radical>woman</radical> reaches the door, ready to leave. A strict house rule ends up <radical>stopping</radical> her before nine. She sighs and stays inside, still somebody's <kanji>daughter</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Jou is how the neighbours refer to her, drawn out and a shade too formal — 「<reading>じょう</reading>」. It is the address for a girl of good family who is not allowed out tonight. She hears じょう and rolls her eyes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>assembly</radical> that has to be held halfway up a <radical>hill</radical> tells you the ground there is <kanji>precipitous</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Guarding that narrow ledge is <reading>Ken</reading>, the shiba who never leaves his wall of antique swords. Every hiker who nears the edge gets one warning bark of <reading>けん</reading> before he bares a blade in his teeth.
items.description: Beyond the literal steep-cliff picture, this kanji usually carries a broader sense of danger or risk in real vocabulary — insurance, adventure, hazard — rather than physical steepness itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Bringing an <radical>axe</radical> down on a standing bundle of <radical>rice</radical> stalks makes a very clean <kanji>severance</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisherman named <reading>Dan</reading> stands at the riverbank when his line goes slack. He shouts <reading>だん</reading> — the exact sound of a taut line snapping in half, sharp and final.

items.mnemonic_text: A flag (方 side) rallying an arrow's (矢) clan together: family.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji>clan</kanji> is everyone who aims an <radical>arrow</radical> in whatever <radical>direction</radical> the <radical>chevron</radical> at the top of the war banner is tilted.
items.reading_mnemonic: Uncle <reading>Zock</reading> has made himself head of the whole clan and lines every cousin up behind his banner on the mountain trail. A gust off the peak sends a shudder down the family, <reading>ぞく</reading>, <reading>ぞく</reading>, one relative after the next. He won't break formation, so the shivering just loops back to the front.
items.description: This character almost never stands alone. It works as a suffix on the end of a compound, marking a group bound by blood or by kind: a household, a tribe, an ethnic people, a band of nobles. Read it as 'the ... folk' rather than a word you say by itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Growing one <radical>violet</radical> on nothing but the <radical>power</radical> of habit is what <kanji>diligence</kanji> looks like.
items.reading_mnemonic: Everyone on the trail just calls the porter <reading>Kin</reading> — not his real name, just the sound he wheezes at the summit every morning: a worn-out <reading>きん</reading>. Then he drops the crate and turns straight back down for the next load.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>wide box</radical> of a room, shoved to the back with <radical>rice</radical> and something <radical>big</radical> on top. You walk through every room to reach it; nobody outside the family does. The deepest room is the <kanji>heart</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ou is the grandmother who lives in that back room and has not come out in years. Knock and you get one long syllable through the paper door — 「<reading>おう</reading>」 — meaning she heard you and no, you may not come in. おう, from the very back of the house.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>cult</radical> that promises <radical>to fill</radical> your storehouse by spring is selling you a <kanji>blessing</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The monk insists it isn't a <reading>fluke</reading>: that same shrine cat has picked the luckiest fortune four mornings running. <reading>ふく</reading>, he mutters, chalking another tally on the gate, certain the cat is hoarding it all for itself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> kneels on the wet <radical>ground</radical> as <radical>rain</radical> pours down. A clerk presses his <radical>stamp</radical> on the puddle, and the ink washes away. Nothing is left to count, so he writes <kanji>zero</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Rei is that clerk. She is scrupulously polite about it — a small bow, a murmured 「<reading>れい</reading>」 — and then she inks the nothing into your row and moves down the line. れい, bow, zero. She has done it forty times today.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Deep in a <radical>thicket</radical> where every other <radical>person</radical> is hidden, the only one I can still point to is <kanji>me</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Lost in that same thicket, a hiker finally crashes out into the open, hugging one soggy paperback <reading>book</reading> to his chest. When the ranger asks whose it is, all he can gasp between breaths is <reading>ぼく</reading> — mine, that one is me.
items.description: As a first-person word this is used mainly by boys and men and stays casual, so it is out of place in formal writing or when you must be very polite. It grew out of an older, humble word for a servant.

items.meaning_mnemonic: This is the <radical>meat</radical> radical and the <kanji>meat</kanji> kanji at once, one shape doing both jobs, so you already know it from the butcher's-shop window.
items.reading_mnemonic: Regulars at the butcher counter groan his name, 「<reading>にく</reading>」, every time <reading>Nick, ooh</reading> leans a thumb on the scale and the <kanji>meat</kanji> jumps a whole kilo.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A farmer beats the stalks until grains burst free across the barn floor. He piles every scattered <radical>rice</radical> grain into one heap. Merchants weigh the heap and ship it out as sacks of <kanji>rice</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A backpacker named <reading>Bay</reading> wanders into the granary and scoops up a handful of the scattered grain. He tastes it raw, eyes wide, and moans a long <reading>べい</reading>, like it's the best thing he's eaten all trip.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Nail a plank of <radical form="木">tree</radical> across a wobbly little <radical form="几">table</radical> so the teacup stops sliding off, and you have built a <kanji form="机">desk</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> the spirit still lives inside that wooden plank, so every time you lean on the <kanji form="机">desk</kanji> to write, she giggles 「<reading>き</reading>」 under your elbows.

items.mnemonic_text: A mouth over stopping legs: a foot that carries you.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> sits on top of a pair of legs. The legs have skidded to a halt — they are <radical>stopping</radical> hard. They end in one part: a <radical>foot</radical>. That's your <kanji>foot</kanji>, your leg, plenty to stand on.
items.reading_mnemonic: The walking mouth named <reading>Sock</reading> skids to such a hard stop that the sock flies off its <kanji form="足">foot</kanji>, and it yelps 「<reading>そく</reading>」 at its bare toes.
items.description: Means foot, leg, or to suffice/be enough; shows up in words for body parts and in verbs about having sufficient amounts.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Even after one <radical>slash</radical> leaves the <radical>samurai</radical> a <radical>body</radical> flat on the tatami, what carries across the hall is the <kanji>voice</kanji> that still shouts orders.
items.reading_mnemonic: Flat on the tatami after the slash, the samurai still shouts 「<reading>せい</reading>」, <reading>say</reading> it, to <reading>Sei</reading> the star student, and his <kanji form="声">voice</kanji> carries to her at the back of the hall.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="卯">rabbit</radical> bends both long ears down around one round <radical form="丶">drop</radical> to keep it warm, because that drop is her <kanji form="卵">egg</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: When a fox sniffs at the nest, long-eared <reading>Ran</reading> squeaks 「<reading>らん</reading>」 and <reading>run</reading>s for it, the <kanji form="卵">egg</kanji> still wobbling between her bent ears.

items.mnemonic_text: A rice field (田) marked out into a town.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>town</kanji> springs up wherever a <radical>street</radical> pushes far enough into the <radical>rice field</radical> that farmers start building shops along both sides of it.
items.reading_mnemonic: A food cart rolls down the new town's one street, and the driver bangs a bell that goes <reading>ちょう</reading> to call the farmers in from the paddies for <reading>chow</reading>. Miss that clang and lunch is gone, so everyone drops their tools the second they hear <reading>ちょう</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A carpenter drags his <radical>angle</radical> gauge to every crooked joint on a birdhouse. Thirty degrees here, ninety there, no two joints match. He shrugs and calls every mismatched joint a perfect <kanji>angle</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the workshop, the carpenter's uncle, always in a <reading>khaki</reading> jacket, grabs the gauge to fix the leaning birdhouse himself. He measures one corner, grunts <reading>かく</reading>, and nails it anyway, angle be damned. It still leans, but now it leans in his signature khaki style.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical form="孚">sincere</radical> hand feeds the small child first and the swan only <radical form="乙">second</radical>, so the swan gets the last drops of <kanji form="乳">milk</kanji> in the bottle.
items.reading_mnemonic: Still hungry, the swan <reading>Nyu</reading> taps the empty bottle with her bent neck and honks 「<reading>にゅう</reading>」 until someone opens a <reading>new</reading> carton of <kanji form="乳">milk</kanji> just for her.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <radical>step</radical> turns into a wild <radical>run</radical> down the road. There is no horse or cart anywhere in sight. So the whole trip happens <kanji>on foot</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Toto the door-to-door turtle has never once taken a ride. He carries the sample doors on his shell and walks the entire round, and he announces himself at every house with the same syllable before he knocks — 「<reading>と</reading>」. と, and another mile.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Pour plain <radical form="氵">water</radical> into a <radical form="酉">sake jar</radical> and leave it overnight, and the jar is so used to its job that by morning the water has become <kanji form="酒">sake</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: All night <reading>Shu</reading> the innkeeper guards the lidded pot, hissing 「<reading>しゅ</reading>」 like <reading>shush</reading> at anyone who walks past, so it can turn into <kanji form="酒">sake</kanji> in peace.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>fish</kanji> is the only animal that will <radical>crouch</radical> in a flooded <radical>rice field</radical> until the water is gone and the <radical>fire</radical> is licking the bottom of the pan.
items.reading_mnemonic: A rockhound in the flooded rice field cracks open a <reading>geode</reading>, and the <kanji form="魚">fish</kanji> crouching beside her leaps up with a startled <reading>ぎょ</reading>, straight into the hot pan.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave a ripe <radical form="果">fruit</radical> lying in the hot <radical form="艹">grass</radical> all summer and the sun cooks it down into a sticky lump of <kanji form="菓">candy</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kaa</reading> the crow is too greedy to wait all summer, so he lets out one fiery <reading>caw</reading>, 「<reading>か</reading>」, and cooks the lump into <kanji form="菓">candy</kanji> on the spot.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The bag that has to <radical form="垂">droop</radical> from the carrier's shoulder at every door in the <radical form="阝">village</radical> is the bag stuffed with <kanji form="郵">mail</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Yuu</reading> the carrier pulls a letter from her sagging bag at each door and shouts 「<reading>ゆう</reading>」, like <reading>you</reading>, because she hands the <kanji form="郵">mail</kanji> to whoever opens first.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>sheep</radical> climbs a <radical>road</radical>, its surface <radical>split</radical> into ruts of packed <radical>earth</radical>. The flock keeps stalling, but the last one clears the rise: the job is <kanji>accomplished</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Tatsu is the drover who marks the top of every hill the same way: one slap on the gatepost and a barked 「<reading>たつ</reading>」 — done, next. He has said it at every gate between here and the coast. たつ means it is finished.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Once your <radical form="口">mouth</radical> makes a <radical form="契">pledge</radical> to clear the whole table, you are stuck having to <kanji form="喫">consume</kanji> every last dish on it.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kit</reading> the goat hears that promise from under the table, bleats 「<reading>きつ</reading>」, and helps you <kanji form="喫">consume</kanji> every dish, then the plates and the tablecloth too.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At a <radical form="巷">fork in the road</radical>, one branch goes on over land and the other ends in the <radical form="氵">water</radical>, so that wet branch is the one that leads to the <kanji form="港">harbor</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Koichi</reading> builds his konbini right where that wet road ends, so his restock boats sail into the <kanji form="港">harbor</kanji> and he waves each one in with a loud 「<reading>こう</reading>」.

items.mnemonic_text: A neck (首) moving down a path: the road and the way.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>road</kanji> is whatever your long <radical>neck</radical> cranes to stare at while your feet <radical>advance</radical>, because you always point your head down the path before you walk it.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Dough</reading> the baker cranes his long neck down the <kanji form="道">road</kanji> before his feet advance a single step, and groans 「<reading>どう</reading>」 at how far his deliveries still have to go.
items.description: Beyond a physical street, 道 also means 'the way' in the sense of a lifelong discipline, which is why it trails the names of pursuits like judo, kendo, and calligraphy.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One <radical form="人">person</radical> opens a roof of cloth on a <radical form="十">cross</radical> of sticks, and the moment <radical form="从">two people</radical> and then <radical form="从">two people</radical> more squeeze under it out of the rain, it is an <kanji form="傘">umbrella</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Even on dry days, <reading>Sunny</reading> pops open that crowded <kanji form="傘">umbrella</kanji> and yells 「<reading>さん</reading>」 at the <reading>sun</reading>, and four strangers still pile under it out of habit.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="木">tree</radical> that grows a <radical form="奇">strange</radical> flat seat and four short legs instead of branches is already a <kanji form="椅">chair</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Eeko</reading> the cat sits on that tree's <kanji form="椅">chair</kanji>, and when a fresh twig pokes up through the seat she lets out a sharp 「<reading>い</reading>」, a squeaky <reading>eek</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="腹">abdomen</kanji> is the part of you that makes you <radical form="复">return</radical> to the fridge every time the <radical form="月">moon</radical> comes up.
items.reading_mnemonic: At midnight <reading>Fuku</reading> the raccoon stands in front of the open fridge, pats his round <kanji form="腹">abdomen</kanji> and sighs 「<reading>ふく</reading>」, the only sound a stuffed belly can make.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The white <radical form="土">earth</radical> you heap into a sharp <radical form="𠂉">chevron</radical> on a <radical form="皿">dish</radical>, so one pinch makes any <radical form="口">mouth</radical> pucker, is <kanji form="塩">salt</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Enzo the chef saves the whole pointed white heap for the very <reading>end</reading>, then tips it all into the soup with a happy 「<reading>えん</reading>」, because to him <kanji form="塩">salt</kanji> is how a recipe says the end.

items.meaning_mnemonic: If your job is to put your <radical form="舌">tongue</radical> on <radical form="辛">spicy</radical> peppers all day long, sooner or later you <kanji form="辞">resign</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Gigi</reading> the pepper taster can only hiss 「<reading>じ</reading>」 through her burning lips like a hot pan, so she writes her note to <kanji form="辞">resign</kanji> on a napkin instead.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The spot you point at to mean your <radical form="自">self</radical> is also the spot you push into any box held out <radical form="畀">to give</radical> you, which is why it is your <kanji form="鼻">nose</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>bee</reading> flies out of the gift box and stings you right on the <kanji form="鼻">nose</kanji>, and you yelp 「<reading>び</reading>」 as it swells up like a red ball.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical form="髟">Hair hanging long</radical> enough for a <radical form="友">friend</radical> to braid can only be <kanji form="髪">hair of the head</kanji>, since nobody braids their arm hair.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hattie stuffs the finished braid under three <reading>hats</reading> at once and says 「<reading>はつ</reading>」, because she thinks <kanji form="髪">hair of the head</kanji> should never see daylight.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Workers stack bars of <radical>gold</radical> in the vault. The inspector's boot hits an immovable <radical>stopping</radical> point at one duller bar. She sets that reject aside and calls it <kanji>silver</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The vault inspector introduces herself as <reading>Gin</reading>. She says it the same flat way every time she rejects a bar, <reading>ぎん</reading>, like she's already bored of the job. She's the one who decided, years ago, that silver deserved its own shelf.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A farmer stacks his <radical>beans</radical> on top of a giant <radical>page</radical> torn from his ledger. The stack wobbles and splits into <radical>eight</radical> tumbling piles. One heavy pile crashes down and thumps him square on the <kanji>head</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the desk, a deskmate spots the bump swelling where the log struck. He winces and mutters <reading>とう</reading>, the same hiss you'd make after stubbing your <reading>toe</reading> on a desk leg.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The dragon at the old <radical form="唐">T'ang</radical> festival keeps its mouth shut on plain <radical form="米">rice</radical>, so the cooks boil the rice down until it turns into sticky <kanji form="糖">sugar</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The festival pot tips over, and the dragon's back-leg dancer, <reading>Toe</reading>, walks off with <kanji form="糖">sugar</kanji> glued to every toe, wailing 「<reading>とう</reading>」 at each sticky step.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Cut down a <radical form="木">tree</radical> as <radical form="喬">high</radical> as a tower, let it fall across the river, and you have a <kanji form="橋">bridge</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A toll-keeper named <reading>Key-oh</reading> has put a padlock on the fallen trunk, and nobody crosses his <kanji form="橋">bridge</kanji> until he jangles his one key and shouts 「<reading>きょう</reading>」.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Because a <radical>lad</radical> this vain only ever grooms the side of his <radical>head</radical> that people see, every hair on his <kanji>face</kanji> is perfect and the back is a mess.
items.reading_mnemonic: The vain lad aims his comb like a <reading>gun</reading> and fires 「<reading>がん</reading>」 at every hair on his <kanji form="顔">face</kanji>, while the back of his head, which nobody sees, stays a mess.

items.mnemonic_text: Three flowing lines of a running river.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>river</radical> radical and the <kanji>river</kanji> kanji are the same character, drawn as the same three flowing strokes every single time.
items.reading_mnemonic: A courier crouches at the riverbank, certain the fastest way to <reading>send</reading> a parcel across is to float it. The current takes it the instant it touches the water and skims it away downstream, hissing <reading>せん</reading> over the shallows.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (大) with a line above their head: the heavens.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One flat <radical>ground</radical> line laid above the arms of the <radical>big</radical> outstretched person turns everything higher than it into <kanji>heaven</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Out on the school sports field, the gym teacher the kids call <reading>Ten</reading> makes the whole class lie flat on the ground. Arms flung out wide, faces up at the open sky, nobody moves. He walks the rows counting slowly, and the drill ends when he reaches <reading>てん</reading>.
items.description: The one to watch is 大, meaning big. 天 has two horizontal strokes stacked at the top, while 大 has just the single crossbar for the arms. That short top line is the whole difference.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>dog</kanji> is a <radical>big</radical> animal so shapeless that the single wet <radical>drop</radical> of its nose is the only way to find its front end.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ken</reading> is a <kanji form="犬">dog</kanji> so big and shapeless that guests find his front end only by the wet drop of his nose, which sniffs 「<reading>けん</reading>」 over every sword he collects.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>copy</kanji> is the page you <radical>bestow</radical> on whoever asks while the real one stays hidden under its <radical>cover</radical> the whole time.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk <reading>Shaw</reading> keeps the real page hidden under its cover and hands each visitor who asks a <kanji form="写">copy</kanji>, hissing 「<reading>しゃ</reading>」 if they try to lift the cover.
items.description: This kanji leans toward capturing an image, like a photograph, more than photocopying. It also covers copying text out by hand or describing a scene.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Winter</kanji> is the one season your <radical>trailing foot</radical> drags a strip of <radical>ice</radical> across the floor with every step you take indoors.
items.reading_mnemonic: With every step indoors, the trailing foot drags a strip of ice behind it, and its numb big <reading>toe</reading> moans 「<reading>とう</reading>」, the sound of deep <kanji form="冬">winter</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: Ten (十) mouths (口) of stories passed down: old.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> counts slowly to <radical>ten</radical> every single morning. It has counted so many mornings that the counting itself feels ancient. Something repeated this many times can only be <kanji>old</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every morning Granny <reading>Coco</reading> counts slowly to ten again, croaking 「<reading>こ</reading>」 at each number, a ritual she has repeated so long it is as <kanji form="古">old</kanji> as she is.
items.description: Means "old," as in old and worn from age; appears in words about age and antiquity and in the common word for "used/secondhand."

items.meaning_mnemonic: You are so <kanji form="忙">busy</kanji> that the wish candle you lit with your whole <radical form="忄">heart</radical> burns down and is <radical form="亡">deceased</radical> before you find one free minute to make the wish.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Bo</reading> the courier is far too <kanji form="忙">busy</kanji> to slow down, so he sprints past your wish candle yelling 「<reading>ぼう</reading>」 and the wind from his legs blows it out.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> strides forward, then drops into a sudden crouch. They press their <radical>family name</radical> seal onto the <radical>ground</radical> instead of a desk. Bowing that low is what <kanji>lower</kanji> means.
items.reading_mnemonic: Tay, a tortoise whose shell is too heavy to lift, groans <reading>てい</reading> every time he tries to stand. It comes out flat and defeated, like the English word <reading>tay</reading>. He gives up and presses his belly back onto the ground beside the still-bowing person. Down there, low is where he stays.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A traveler <radical form="艮">stopping</radical> mid-step so that one tiny <radical form="丶">drop</radical> of dew can slide off its leaf without being crushed is about as <kanji form="良">good</kanji> as anyone gets.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Leo</reading> barks 「<reading>りょう</reading>」 at the hold-up on the path until he spots the saved dewdrop, then sits down and wags like the <kanji form="良">good</kanji> boy he is.

items.mnemonic_text: Drops falling inside a window frame from the sky: rain.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You already know this one, since the <radical>rain</radical> radical you learned and the <kanji>rain</kanji> kanji are the same character down to the last dash.
items.reading_mnemonic: You're pressed to the shrine window watching the rain streak down the glass, and a puddle of it starts to <reading>ooze</reading> under the door across your socks. Grandma Kane's cats line up and stare at the growing puddle, and every one of them lets out the same low, damp <reading>う</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> steps onto the thawed <radical>ground</radical> after a long winter. They plant <radical>two</radical> sticks and throw their arms out as <radical>big</radical> as they can. The <radical>sun</radical> climbs higher each morning until mud season turns into <kanji>springtime</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A groundhog named <reading>Shun</reading> pokes up from his burrow the moment the yard warms, shouts <reading>しゅん</reading>, and dives straight back down out of pure habit. He shuns the cold on principle, but there isn't any today — the mud outside smells exactly like the springtime the person just stepped into.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> leans over and drops onto the <radical>fire</radical> burning beside the field. It catches fast and sends smoke drifting over the empty rows. That smoky smell means <kanji>autumn</kanji> has arrived.
items.reading_mnemonic: A scarecrow standing in the smoking field flaps its sleeves at circling crows and yells <reading>shoo</reading>, <reading>しゅう</reading>, over and over until they scatter. Smoke from the burning stalks stings its painted eyes, but it keeps shouting anyway — the last of the grain only survives if somebody protects it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Your bare feet scorch on the baked <radical>ground</radical>. You point at <radical>self</radical> and swear the heat does not bother you. Then your <radical>trailing foot</radical> drags behind, and the stubborn heat becomes <kanji>summer</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kaa, the fire-breathing crow, sags on a power line above that same baked ground. Too hot even for him, he cracks his beak and a weak puff of flame escapes with a scorched <reading>か</reading>. That tired flame-cough is how you remember summer's reading, <reading>か</reading>.

items.mnemonic_text: A tall tower with windows: high and expensive.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the flat <radical>prairie</radical>, a lone tower capped with a pot <radical>lid</radical> and pierced by one <radical>mouth</radical> of a window is the only thing for miles, so it looks impossibly <kanji>tall</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Koichi</reading> the konbini king leans out of the one window of the prairie tower, under its pot-lid roof, and yells 「<reading>こう</reading>」 down at the plain, since nothing for miles stands so <kanji form="高">tall</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The falling <radical>rain</radical> freezes solid before it lands outside the temple. A monk grabs a <radical>broom</radical> and sweeps the icy drops into soft white drifts. He won't ring the bell until every trace of <kanji>snow</kanji> is gone.
items.reading_mnemonic: The groundskeeper everyone calls <reading>Set</reading> mutters <reading>せつ</reading> under his breath every time he has to shovel the steps again. By dawn the drifts are back, deeper than before, and so is his sigh.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical form="犭">animal</radical> that flattens every rice <radical form="苗">seedling</radical> in the field by curling up for a nap on top of them is, of course, the <kanji form="猫">cat</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Bee-Owl</reading> swoops low over the field hooting 「<reading>びょう</reading>」 to chase off the napping <kanji form="猫">cat</kanji>, who just rolls over onto a fresh patch of rice.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>bird</radical> radical and the <kanji>bird</kanji> kanji are the same character, and it also means chicken, because a chicken is just the bird you are most likely to eat.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the shrine a fat cat named <reading>Chow</reading> watches the pigeons land and rumbles 「<reading>ちょう</reading>」, since as far as she is concerned a <kanji>bird</kanji> is just lunch that has not noticed her yet.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Koichi forgets an oil lantern burning behind the konbini shelf. All night its glass glows a soft <radical>yellow</radical>, brighter than the fluorescent lights above. By morning the whole shelf is stained <kanji>yellow</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi restocks the shelf by lantern light, counting under his breath: <reading>こう</reading>. It comes out low and steady, exactly like a pigeon's <reading>coo</reading>, over and over until every row is full again.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Nothing in the whole hot, crowded <radical form="京">capital</radical> is as <kanji form="涼">refreshing</kanji> as the cold <radical form="氵">water</radical> in the fountain right inside its giant gate.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Leon</reading> the gate guard sneaks into the fountain sighing 「<reading>りょう</reading>」 and tells his angry captain the water was far too <kanji form="涼">refreshing</kanji> to guard from outside.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="帽">cap</kanji> is just a scrap of <radical form="巾">cloth</radical> on your head that makes looking up at the sky no longer a <radical form="冒">risk</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Beau</reading> the umpire bows so low to the crowd, groaning 「<reading>ぼう</reading>」, that his <kanji form="帽">cap</kanji> drops in the dirt and he squints through the whole last inning.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Rain</radical> falls onto the <radical>ground</radical> where <radical>two</radical> silkworms spin themselves into a <radical>cocoon</radical>. The cocoon soaks up water until it swells and floats free. It drifts upward and puffs into a <kanji>cloud</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: That swollen cocoon keeps drifting away from the ground like a stray <reading>balloon</reading>, and everyone at the window mutters <reading>うん</reading> in surprise as it floats past, still dripping rain.

items.meaning_mnemonic: So much <radical form="氵">water</radical> that even a <radical form="胡">barbarian</radical> rider has to stop his horse and ride all the way around it is a <kanji form="湖">lake</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ko</reading>, a duck no bigger than a shoe, tows the fur-cloaked rider and his whole horse across the <kanji form="湖">lake</kanji> on a rope, puffing 「<reading>こ</reading>」 with every paddle.

items.meaning_mnemonic: It turns <kanji>sultry</kanji> when <radical>someone</radical> is pinned in an open field and the <radical>sun</radical> bakes the damp air around them for hours.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Show</reading> the weatherman does his forecast live from a treeless field, so overheated that the one syllable he can force out, 「<reading>しょ</reading>」, is now the station's official word for a <kanji>sultry</kanji> afternoon.
items.description: This is heat from the air or the weather, not from a hot object. Something hot to the touch, like a pan or a kettle, is written with another kanji entirely.

items.meaning_mnemonic: It is so <kanji>cold</kanji> under the <radical>roof</radical> that the <radical>well</radical> freezes to <radical>ice</radical>, and the swelling ice <radical>splits</radical> the <radical>ground</radical> beneath the house.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the roof, a tin <reading>can</reading> dropped down the well bounces off solid ice with a hollow 「<reading>かん</reading>」, and the ground beneath the house splits wider, it is so <kanji form="寒">cold</kanji>.
items.description: This is the cold you feel all over, from cold weather or an unheated room. A single cold thing you touch, like a drink or a metal rail, is a different kanji.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When two hands wave <radical form="非">not</radical> that one at the last cookie your <radical form="心">heart</radical> wants, the heart has nothing left to do but <kanji form="悲">grieve</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Every time little <reading>Hee</reading> reaches for the last cookie, the two hands wave him away again, so he sits on the floor to <kanji form="悲">grieve</kanji>, sobbing 「<reading>ひ</reading>」 into his sleeve.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Grab the stick the <radical form="日">sun</radical> lowers to you and it will <radical form="爰">lead on to</radical> the top of the sky, close enough to soak up its <kanji form="暖">warmth</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Frozen <reading>Dan</reading> hauls himself up the stick hand over hand, yelling 「<reading>だん</reading>」 at every pull, until the <kanji form="暖">warmth</kanji> up top melts the icicle off his nose.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When you go <radical form="彔">to carve wood</radical> from a fresh young log, the wet chips stain every <radical form="糸">thread</radical> of your shirt <kanji form="緑">green</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Old <reading>Ryoko</reading> picks the wet chips off her shirt one by one, sighing 「<reading>りょく</reading>」 at each new <kanji form="緑">green</kanji> spot that no washing will ever get out.

items.meaning_mnemonic: When the whole street blows horns to <radical form="喜">rejoice</radical>, the <radical form="女">woman</radical> who starts dancing in the middle of it is the one who is truly <kanji form="嬉">glad</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Kiki</reading> leans out of an old tree to watch the dancer spin past, so <kanji form="嬉">glad</kanji> she giggles 「<reading>き</reading>、<reading>き</reading>」 until her branches shake loose a bird's nest.

items.meaning_mnemonic: To keep your <radical form="金">gold</radical> safe you <radical form="建">build</radical> a lock around it, and the one small thing that can open that lock is the <kanji form="鍵">key</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ken</reading> the sword-collecting dog sleeps on top of the safe with its only <kanji form="鍵">key</kanji> held in his teeth, and he growls 「<reading>けん</reading>」 at anyone who reaches for it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Even a patient <radical form="夫">husband</radical> finds it <kanji form="難">difficult</kanji> to push one blade of <radical form="艹">grass</radical> into the clamped <radical form="口">mouth</radical> of a stubborn <radical form="隹">old bird</radical>.
items.reading_mnemonic: His granny <reading>Nan</reading> takes over, hums 「<reading>なん</reading>」 once, and the beak pops open at once, because nothing is <kanji form="難">difficult</kanji> for a granny.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>drop</radical> of water lands on a coiled fishing hook shaped like <radical>nine</radical>. The drop pulls the coil tight around itself as it slides in. It curls shut into a perfect <kanji>round</kanji> ball.
items.reading_mnemonic: The fisherman reeling in that tight round ball grunts <reading>がん</reading> with every heave, a sound as sharp as a rusty <reading>gun</reading> cocking twice. Neighbors on the riverbank swear they can hear it from their porches.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>beginning</kanji> of anyone's story is the <radical>two</radical> marks drawn at the very top, long before the <radical>human legs</radical> below ever carry them anywhere.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Gwen</reading> the storyteller draws the two marks at the very top of a fresh page and says 「<reading>げん</reading>」, because the <kanji form="元">beginning</kanji> must be there before the legs below walk anywhere.
items.description: Not just 'beginning': this character often works as a prefix meaning 'former' or 'ex-,' as in a former teacher or a former boss.

items.mnemonic_text: A shelter (广) opening onto open ground: wide, spacious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A cliffside <radical>shelter</radical> holding nothing but one silkworm's <radical>cocoon</radical> is almost all empty air, so the bare floor stretches out absurdly <kanji>wide</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Koichi</reading> the konbini king peers into the cliffside shelter holding one lone cocoon and murmurs 「<reading>こう</reading>」, already picturing shelves across a floor that <kanji form="広">wide</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical form="氵">Water</radical> that sinks into the <radical form="一">ground</radical> and then gets stuck in a <radical form="丂">kink</radical> of the drain pipe just sits there until it turns <kanji form="汚">dirty</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The plumber Otto pulls the drain pipe straight, takes the whole <kanji form="汚">dirty</kanji> gush in the face, and the only word he has left is <reading>Oh</reading>, 「<reading>お</reading>」.

items.mnemonic_text: A woman (女) beside her child (子): a fondness, to like.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> who will put down anything to pick her <radical>child</radical> back up is the dictionary picture of <kanji>fond</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A mother drops everything she carries to scoop her child back up, and <reading>Koichi</reading>, watching from his till, lets out a soft 「<reading>こう</reading>」 at a sight so <kanji form="好">fond</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>possess</kanji> a thing only while your <radical>left hand</radical> stays clamped on it, which is why even the <radical>moon</radical> becomes yours the second you get a grip.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Hugh</reading> clamps his left hand on the moon and yells 「<reading>ゆう</reading>」, just like <reading>you</reading>, at the crowd below, because only a hand that grips gets to <kanji form="有">possess</kanji> it.

items.mnemonic_text: A box repeating the same shape inside: the same.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When every <radical>mouth</radical> shut inside a <radical>wide box</radical> eats off one flat <radical>ground</radical>, no bowl can be bigger than another, so all their meals come out the <kanji>same</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Inside the wide box, the cook <reading>Dough</reading> drops one ladle onto the flat ground before every shut mouth, grunting 「<reading>どう</reading>」 each time so every meal comes out the <kanji form="同">same</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Hang from the bar across a <radical form="日">sun</radical>-lit window by your <radical form="廾">two hands</radical> every morning, and slowly that straight bar will <kanji form="曲">bend</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fat pigeon called <reading>Kyo-coo</reading> also sits on that window bar each morning, coos 「<reading>きょく</reading>」, and makes it <kanji form="曲">bend</kanji> a little more.

items.meaning_mnemonic: After <radical form="十">ten</radical> chilies you can no longer sit, so you <radical form="立">stand</radical> up and hop around the table, which is how you know the soup is <kanji form="辛">spicy</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Hopping around the table after his own <kanji form="辛">spicy</kanji> soup, the cook Shinji cracks his <reading>shin</reading> on a table leg and howls 「<reading>しん</reading>！」

items.mnemonic_text: A dying (亡) heart (心) losing its memory: to forget.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a name you loved slips under the lid and joins the <radical>deceased</radical>, your <radical>heart</radical> keeps beating but you <kanji>forget</kanji> it was ever there.
items.reading_mnemonic: You give the grave a slow, deep <reading>bow</reading>, back creaking 「<reading>ぼう</reading>」, and as you rise your heart beats on but you <kanji form="忘">forget</kanji> whose name went under the lid.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical form="艹">grass</radical> your <radical form="右">right</radical> hand can pull out with no effort at all is the soft, <kanji form="若">young</kanji> kind.
items.reading_mnemonic: The gardener <reading>Jack</reading> pulls up only the <kanji form="若">young</kanji> shoots because one tug is enough, yet he still yanks so hard he falls on his back, yelling 「<reading>じゃく</reading>」.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical form="犭">animal</radical> that tries to nap inside your <radical form="夹">sandwich</radical> has bread pressed against both sides and finds it very <kanji form="狭">cramped</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Pressed flat between the slices of bread in that <kanji form="狭">cramped</kanji> lunch, the ferret <reading>Kyo</reading> squeaks 「<reading>きょう</reading>」 every time you take a bite.

items.mnemonic_text: Two bent bows losing their tension: weak.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Draw the string on a <radical>bow</radical> carved from <radical>ice</radical> and it snaps in your hand, because a frozen weapon is a <kanji>weak</kanji> one.
items.reading_mnemonic: Archer <reading>Jack</reading> draws his bow carved from ice, it snaps in his hands, and he groans 「<reading>じゃく</reading>」 at a frozen weapon this <kanji form="弱">weak</kanji>.
items.description: Tacked onto the end of a number, this kanji flips from 'weak' to 'a little under'. A count with it on the tail means just below that figure, not a feeble version of it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>rouse</kanji> <radical>oneself</radical> at dawn only by making your legs <radical>run</radical> for the door before the rest of you gets a vote.
items.reading_mnemonic: At dawn <reading>Kiki</reading> the tree spirit shrieks 「<reading>き</reading>」 at your legs, and they <kanji form="起">rouse</kanji> you by running for the door before the rest of you gets a vote.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Staring across a <radical form="谷">valley</radical> at the rice ball on the far side, the one thing you <radical form="欠">lack</radical>, is exactly what <kanji form="欲">longing</kanji> feels like.
items.reading_mnemonic: A tiny chick called <reading>Yolk</reading> peeps 「<reading>よく</reading>」 from the cliff edge at that rice ball all day, too small to jump across and too full of <kanji form="欲">longing</kanji> to leave.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Lock a <radical form="才">genius</radical> kid inside a <radical form="門">gate</radical> and the doors stay <kanji form="閉">closed</kanji>, because he already knows every trick you will try to open them.
items.reading_mnemonic: A horse named <reading>Hay</reading> neighs 「<reading>へい</reading>」 at the doors all night for his dinner, but the kid inside just smiles and keeps them <kanji form="閉">closed</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The night <radical form="兑">exchange</radical> under the <radical form="月">moon</radical> trades your day clothes for pajamas, but only once you <kanji form="脱">undress</kanji> right there at the counter.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk at that counter, a ladybug called <reading>Dots</reading>, taps the sign and says 「<reading>だつ</reading>」 until you <kanji form="脱">undress</kanji>, then hands you pajamas covered in dots.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>arrow</radical> hits a target and snaps in half, the pieces splitting apart like <radical>eight</radical>. The stub falls into a bowl of <radical>beans</radical> and looks tiny beside a whole one. Cut off before its time, the little arrow stays <kanji>short</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The vendor is a wiry guy everyone calls <reading>Tan</reading>. Every time he pulls another snapped stub from the bowl, he mutters <reading>たん</reading> under his breath. He's annoyed at how short his profits look today.
items.description: Beyond literal shortness, 短 also carries the sense of a shortcoming. It's the kind of short that comes up when someone lists a personality flaw or weak point, not just a measurement of length.

items.mnemonic_text: A cart (車) that passes lightly (圣): not heavy.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>holy</radical> hand laid flat on a loaded <radical>vehicle</radical> draws the weight out like a blessing, until the <kanji>light (weight)</kanji> cart drifts a finger off the road.
items.reading_mnemonic: A kid named <reading>Kay</reading> runs after the blessed cart as it drifts down the road a finger off the ground. Every time it bobs higher she shouts <reading>けい</reading>, which is her own name and the exact sound Japanese gives the letter K.

items.mnemonic_text: Learning (⺍) opening one's view (見): to remember, realize.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>remember</kanji> a <radical>small</radical> fact by tucking it under a <radical>cover</radical> where your roving eye can still <radical>see</radical> the lump it makes.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the shrine, Grandma Kane keeps the one phone number she still needs tucked under a sleeping cat's blanket. Each time she lifts the cover, checks it, and finds she still knows it, she gives a dry <reading>かく</reading>. That is the small <reading>cackle</reading> of someone glad her mind still works.
items.description: The active side of remember, closer to memorize or learn by heart than to passive recall.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Shove a <radical>bench</radical> sideways into the mouth of a <radical>gate</radical> and the heavy doors can never swing shut, so the courtyard stays <kanji>open</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Doorman <reading>Kai</reading> cannot say his own name without flinging both arms wide, so every time he answers 「<reading>かい</reading>」 the doors behind him bang <kanji>open</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: Sheep (羊) settling onto the eye's (目) view: to arrive, to wear.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Cut one <radical>slash</radical> down a whole <radical>sheep</radical>, pull the fleece around you until it hides an <radical>eye</radical>, and you <kanji>wear</kanji> the animal itself.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki, the tree spirit, giggles inside her old oak while you wrestle into the fresh sheep-fleece coat. She pokes a branch out and gives the hem one hard <reading>chuck</reading> downward to seat it on your shoulders, laughing <reading>ちゃく</reading> as the collar flops over your eyes.
items.description: One character, two senses that feel unrelated: to put on or wear clothing, and to arrive at or reach a place. The wear sense uses the kun reading; the arrive sense shows up in travel words for arrival and landing. It is normal to be thrown that the same character means both.

items.mnemonic_text: A wandering road (辶) with a flag (斿) of fun: to play.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Drifting like a <radical>swim</radical>mer down whatever <radical>road</radical> opens next, with no place you have to be, is exactly <kanji>play</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: After the last bell a kid called <reading>Yu</reading> never walks straight home. His friends stand out on the sports field yelling <reading>ゆう</reading> until he drifts over to whichever game is loudest. One game bleeds into the next, and that is his whole afternoon, every afternoon.

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) hidden behind sound (音) of night: dark.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A room with its <radical>sun</radical> switched off, where you steer only by <radical>sound</radical>, is the very definition of <kanji>dark</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ann, the mole, shuffles across the pitch-black room feeling along the wall until she finds the switch marked <reading>on</reading>. She flicks it again and again and nothing happens, so she groans <reading>あん</reading> and goes back to steering by sound in the total dark.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical form="女">woman</radical> made to perform two different dances <radical form="兼">concurrently</radical> soon starts to <kanji form="嫌">dislike</kanji> both of them.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Ken</reading> the sword-collecting dog barks 「<reading>けん</reading>」 and tosses the dancer a sword to juggle as well, and she shows her <kanji form="嫌">dislike</kanji> by throwing it straight back at his wall.

items.meaning_mnemonic: To <kanji form="寝">lie down</kanji> under a <radical form="宀">roof</radical>, stretch out on the half log of the <radical form="爿">left-side kata</radical>, pull a <radical form="冖">cover</radical> over all but your <radical form="⺕">snout</radical>, and tug it up <radical form="又">again</radical> whenever it slips.
items.reading_mnemonic: A raccoon named <reading>Shin</reading> tries to <kanji form="寝">lie down</kanji> on that half log, but the blanket only reaches his knees, so his bare shin sticks out and he squeaks 「<reading>しん</reading>」 all night.

items.mnemonic_text: A person (亻) in motion (動): working.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one <radical>person</radical> still on the <radical>move</radical> after the whole group has flopped down in the shade is the only one actually doing <kanji>work</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine, she settles in among the cats while the one helper she calls <reading>Dough</reading> sweeps every mossy step, polishes the giant bell, and refills all the lanterns by himself. Each heave on the bell-hammer drags a tired <reading>どう</reading> out of him.
items.description: This is one of a small set of kanji coined in Japan, not borrowed from China. It adds the person radical to the 'move' character, the idea being that a person in motion is a person at work.

items.mnemonic_text: A hand over a mouth, the right hand that feeds you.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Once your <radical>left hand</radical> is busy holding the bowl, the only hand free to lift food to your <radical>mouth</radical> is your <kanji>right</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A fisherman named <reading>Woo</reading> eats his lunch at the riverbank one-handed, his left hand still gripping the oar, and his clumsy right keeps dropping rice down his shirt until he lets out a long <reading>う</reading>. Every lost mouthful earns another flat <reading>う</reading>.
items.description: The look-alikes are 左 (left) and 石 (stone). All three place a shape beneath a hand-like top. In 右 that top is a short slant crossing a short flat stroke, with 口 right under it. 左 keeps the same top. Its lower part is a narrow shape with a flat foot, not a closed box. 石 keeps the 口 underneath. Its top stroke stretches into one long flat overhang with a square corner, like a cliff.

items.mnemonic_text: A hand over a craftsman's tool, held in the left hand.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your flat <radical>left hand</radical> exists to hold the <radical>construction</radical> girder still while your other hand does the bolting, so <kanji>left</kanji> just means the bracing hand.
items.reading_mnemonic: Sara steadies the construction beam with her left hand, exactly as that hand is built to do, and drives the saw with her right. Every stroke drags a dry <reading>さ</reading> out of the plank, the flat sound of a <reading>saw</reading> in soft pine. She keeps going until the whole site is ankle deep in sawdust.
items.description: The look-alike is 右, meaning right. Both share the flat left-hand stroke across the top; the giveaway sits underneath, where left carries the construction beam and right holds a small closed box instead. In left the horizontal top stroke is the long one, while in right the slanting stroke is longer and the horizontal stays short.

items.mnemonic_text: Two people back to back turning away from the cold north.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Here is one that comes free, because the <radical>north</radical> radical and the <kanji>north</kanji> kanji are the very same character, learned once and counted twice.
items.reading_mnemonic: Down at the frozen riverbank, two skaters stand back to back and guard the same net. Every time the puck clangs off the post they both bark <reading>ほく</reading>, the flat grunt a rink announcer makes yelling <reading>hockey</reading> into a dead microphone.

items.mnemonic_text: Bad luck (歹) beside a person collapsed: to die.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When your <radical>bad luck</radical> runs deep enough to bend the <radical>spoon</radical> before it reaches your lips, the next thing you do is <kanji>die</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nurse <reading>Shh</reading> sees the spoon bend before it reaches the patient's lips and hisses 「<reading>し</reading>」 at the ward, because luck that bad means he is about to <kanji form="死">die</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A bird settling into its nest as the sun sets in the west.
items.meaning_mnemonic: No new work here, because the <radical>west</radical> radical, that sun climbing down into its crate for the night, is the <kanji>west</kanji> kanji with not one stroke moved.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the school, when the teacher asks which way the sun goes down, Sei's hand is up before anyone has even finished hearing the question. Too pleased with himself to wait his turn, he leans back and says <reading>せい</reading>. It is the right answer, because that is the sound you <reading>say</reading> for west.
items.description: The look-alike is 四, meaning four. West has a separate horizontal lid across the very top that pokes out past the sides, and the two upright strokes inside rise up to meet it. Four is a plain sealed rectangle with a flat top and no overhang, and its two inner strokes curl apart at the bottom without touching the top.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>England</kanji> is the one country where a flawless patch of <radical>grass</radical> mown at the dead <radical>center</radical> of the garden counts as a national achievement.
items.reading_mnemonic: The tour guide <reading>Amy</reading> kneels by the flawless patch of grass at the dead centre of the garden and gasps 「<reading>えい</reading>」, and all of <kanji form="英">England</kanji> applauds the mowing.
items.description: Beyond the country name, this kanji means outstanding or brilliant, as in words for a hero or a gifted person. England just borrows its sound.

items.mnemonic_text: The sun (日) tangled in a tree (木): sunrise in the east.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture the <radical>sun</radical> rising and getting tangled in the branches of a <radical>tree</radical> on the horizon. You see the sun caught right behind that tree first thing in the morning — and the sun always comes up in the east. Sun plus tree, hung together at dawn: that's <kanji>east</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the top of the mountain trail, a hiker faces the sunrise and lets out a long, tired yawn — a huge "<reading>とう</reading>" that echoes down the slope. Every morning she climbs to greet the east with that same sleepy とう.

items.mnemonic_text: A warm shelter facing the sunny south.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two <radical>horns</radical> poke out of a <radical>wide box</radical> lashed to the only wall that stays <radical>dry</radical> and warm through <radical>ten</radical> winters, and a wall like that faces <kanji>south</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nan sets her deck chair against the south wall of the barn each morning, beside the old crate with the horns poking out. Ask why she never sits on the shady north side and she grumbles that it gets <reading>なん</reading> of the afternoon sun, dragging the word out as she tips her hat down. Everyone just calls her <reading>Nan</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A dockhand splits a log into <radical>eight</radical> pieces with one swing. He wedges them along the hull of a <radical>boat</radical> to patch a leak. Then he bolts on a hatch shaped like a <radical>mouth</radical>, finishing his little <kanji>ship</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Down at the dock, the sailor <reading>Sen</reading> hears the hatch slam onto his thumb and hisses a long <reading>せん</reading> through his teeth, hopping on one foot as the boat rocks against the pier.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> ducks into a silk shed as a <radical>cocoon</radical> splits open. She pulls out <radical>two</radical> threads and crosses them on a frame. The tangled <radical>thread</radical> slowly becomes a <kanji>picture</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The embroiderer everyone calls <reading>Kai</reading> signs every finished piece with his initial stitched in the corner: a tiny looped <reading>かい</reading>. Collectors say you can spot his work from across the room, that little loop of thread is his signature every time.

items.mnemonic_text: Feet advancing (辶) among matched (巽) options: to choose.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When the trail forks and you may <radical>advance</radical> down only one branch, taking the <radical>southeast</radical> fork instead of all the others is exactly what it means to <kanji>choose</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the fork in the trail, a guide named <reading>Sen</reading> taps the southeast branch and says 「<reading>せん</reading>」, because somebody has to <kanji form="選">choose</kanji> before the hikers lose the light.

items.mnemonic_text: A boxed shape holding the round yen coin.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>stick</radical> pinned at one end to the <radical>ground</radical> and swung all the way around the inside of a <radical>wide box</radical> scratches out the round coin you spend as one <kanji>yen</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The monk <reading>Zen</reading> pins the stick to the ground and swings it round inside the wide box, murmuring 「<reading>えん</reading>」 as the scratched circle becomes one <kanji form="円">yen</kanji> coin.
