items.meaning_mnemonic: In Koichi's konbini, a customer catches his own reflection in the till's dark screen. On the left he stands upright, a normal <radical>person</radical>; on the right that body has folded double and sprouted a stubby tail. One shape slides into the other, mid-blink: <kanji>change</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Outside the window, Kaa the fire-breathing crow has been watching the whole trick from the power line. He can't hold it in — he lets out a hoarse <reading>か</reading>, the same rasp as his name, <reading>Kaa</reading>, and a puff of flame scorches the wire above the sliding doors.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A hiker finds a boxy frame with crossed bars beside the trail. Curious, she puts it to <radical>use</radical>, feeding it coins for tea. Even on a bare mountain, someone found a way to <kanji>utilize</kanji> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the summit vending machine, a hiker named <reading>Yo</reading> finally gets her drink and lets out a long, relieved yodel: <reading>よう</reading>, echoing off the ridge. The machine rattles once more, empty and satisfied with its work.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>ray</kanji> is a <radical>small</radical> bright speck set on a <radical>flat top</radical> so level that it can throw one line dead straight for miles without ever dipping.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Koichi</reading> sets a small bright speck on the dead-level flat top of his konbini counter, says 「<reading>こう</reading>」, and its <kanji form="光">ray</kanji> shoots out the door straight for miles.

items.mnemonic_text: Grasping (⺈) at the heart (心): an urgent hurry.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji>hurry</kanji> when a pounding <radical>heart</radical> drives you into a low <radical>crouch</radical> with your <radical>snout</radical> already aimed at the door.
items.reading_mnemonic: Your heart pounds and you drop into a low crouch with your snout at the door, so when <reading>Cue</reading> the starter yells 「<reading>きゅう</reading>」, you <kanji form="急">hurry</kanji> out.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>rice field</radical> so tightly <radical>jammed in</radical> by fences on every side becomes its own private <kanji>world</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A surveyor named <reading>Kai</reading> barks 「<reading>かい</reading>」 each time her tape measure claims another field, and she will not rest until the whole <kanji>world</kanji> is fenced into tidy squares.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>woman</radical> drops a bag of <radical>rice</radical> and grains spill everywhere. Her <radical>trailing foot</radical> drags them into neat <radical>chevron</radical> stripes. She <radical>taps</radical> each stripe with her toe to find the final <kanji>number</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back in that gym, the scorekeeper — a woman named <reading>Sue</reading> — squints at the tally and groans <reading>すう</reading>, dragging the sound out like she dreads the total. The same scattered rice still crunches under her shoes.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>bird</radical> lands on the goalpost during recess. Its beak opens into a wide <radical>mouth</radical> like a square hole. Out comes a piercing <kanji>chirp</kanji> that stops the game.
items.reading_mnemonic: The gym teacher on duty is called <reading>May</reading>. She blows her whistle and shouts <reading>めい</reading> every time that shriek cuts through practice. Nobody on the field mentions that the bird started it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>construction</radical> radical and the <kanji>craft</kanji> kanji are the same, and since raising a building takes the same skilled hands as any other craft, one character does for both.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi pulls on a carpenter's <reading>coat</reading> to guide the steel beam down between the two concrete slabs, barking a proud 「<reading>こう</reading>」 as it lands, because that is real <kanji form="工">craft</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Walk <radical>one</radical> straight line and <radical>stop</radical> exactly on the mark to be counted <kanji>correct</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back in the classroom, the teacher asks who stopped exactly on the line. Sei's hand shoots up before she finishes asking, and he answers with his own name like it settles it: <reading>Sei</reading>, <reading>せい</reading> — crisp, correct, a little too pleased with himself.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Lay a <radical>shield</radical> flat on the ground and its face gives you a surface that is perfectly <kanji>even</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A hiker drags himself into the clearing, drops his pack, and lets out one long <reading>hey</reading>. That flat exhale is exactly the sound of <reading>へい</reading>: level, calm, done.

items.meaning_mnemonic: One <radical>eye</radical> on each side of a <radical>tree</radical>, each watching the other, is exactly what <kanji>inter</kanji>action looks like.

items.mnemonic_text: A heart (心) pierced by a single resolved stroke: certainly necessary.

items.description: The look-alike is 心, heart or mind. 心 is the bare heart shape, a wide low curve with three loose dots and nothing crossing it. 必 adds one straight slash cutting from the upper right down through the middle, and that diagonal is the whole difference.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>mouth</radical> shouts a price for a crate of <radical>goods</radical> in the crowded market. Another mouth shouts back an even higher price. By closing time both have sold every last one of their <kanji>goods</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: An inspector named <reading>Hin</reading> arrives to stamp the stacked crates before they ship. Top crate: a short, sharp <reading>ひん</reading>. Left crate: <reading>ひん</reading>. Right crate: <reading>ひん</reading>. Three stamps, three crates, one approved delivery.
items.description: 品 covers more than merchandise. It can also mean refined bearing or quiet dignity — the sense behind calling someone classy rather than crude. That reading has nothing to do with boxes, so expect 品 to describe character as often as cargo.

items.description: 組 pictures strands twisted into a braid, and that same image stretches to any group bound together the same way — a class, a team, a pair of chopsticks — so association here means an interlocking set, not a loose informal gathering.

items.mnemonic_text: Legs launching outward from a bow: departure, emitting.

The racer's <radical>human legs</radical> land planted wide just as <radical>two</radical> chopsticks clatter off a dropped bento — chasing a train already <kanji>departed</kanji>, hissing steam as it pulls away without them.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Water</radical> loosening every <radical>tongue</radical> in the room is what turns a quiet evening <kanji>lively</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The commuter jolts upright and sneezes so hard he headbutts the shelf — a violent <reading>ka-choo</reading> that comes out sounding exactly like <reading>かつ</reading>, onigiri raining down around him. Koichi just restocks the shelf and waits for the next customer to keel over the same way.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 問 as a <radical>gate</radical> with a <radical>mouth</radical> built into the crossbar, shouting through the bars at Sei's school. They let out one long identical <reading>moan</reading> that comes out as <reading>もん</reading>, echoing off the bars, and they're still moaning it when the gate creaks open.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Bamboo</radical> rods laid under one <radical>eye</radical> and <radical>two hands</radical> is the oldest way anybody found to <kanji>calculate</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>topic</kanji> is the single <radical>right</radical> word that has to sit in a chapter's <radical>head</radical>ing.

items.description: Beyond topic, this is the ordinary character for the title of a book or film and for an exam or homework question. All three senses share one idea: what the thing is about.

items.description: 怪 carries more than a raised eyebrow of doubt — it's the character behind monsters, ghost stories, and the eerie unknown, so think uncanny and unexplained before you think of doubting someone's alibi.

The verb sense stretch or spread is the same idea: pulling something tight, which is why the same character became the counting word for anything strung that way.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>rice field</radical> radical and the <kanji>rice field</kanji> kanji are the same character, which as a full kanji widens from the plot symbol to the whole flooded paddy those dirt paths chop into green squares.

He points and wails <reading>だい</reading>, landing like the English word <reading>dye</reading> spilled across the square. The ground trembles with every sob. The straw substitute never even flinches.

items.meaning_mnemonic: To <kanji>polish</kanji> a sword you drag its blade back and forth across a flat <radical>stone</radical> propped on a steady <radical>bench</radical> until it shines back at you.
items.reading_mnemonic: No sword goes back on the wall until <reading>Ken</reading> the sword-collecting dog has <kanji>polish</kanji>ed it to a mirror, and he growls 「<reading>けん</reading>」 at every last smudge.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Under a <radical>cliff</radical>, a peddler takes her <radical>stand</radical> guarding a pot with a <radical>lid</radical>. A shoot of <radical>life</radical> pushes up and splits it into <radical>eight</radical> pieces. By morning her stall overflows with <kanji>products</kanji>.

items.mnemonic_text: A bird (隹) landing on a tree (木) with the flock: to gather.

items.reading_mnemonic: A photographer blurts 「<reading>しゅう</reading>」, his way of saying <reading>shoot</reading>, as every stiff old bird hops over to <kanji form="集">gather</kanji> on the one low-branched tree for the group photo.

items.mnemonic_text: Words (言) matched all around (周): to check, investigate.

items.reading_mnemonic: Detective <reading>Cho</reading> only calls a case truly <kanji>investigate</kanji>d once he has looped the entire block yelling 「<reading>ちょう</reading>」 at every door, since anything less leaves a gap in the circle.
items.description: The common verb here means 'look something up' or 'check' — a word, a timetable, a fact — as often as it means a formal investigation.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A painter drops a spool of <radical>white</radical> <radical>thread</radical> into a bucket of <radical>water</radical>. The water pulls it taut in one direction. It stretches into one straight <kanji>line</kanji> across the floor.
items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream, lifeguard <reading>Sen</reading> blows her whistle every time that white string drifts off course, barking <reading>せん</reading> until the swimmers straighten back into the lane she marked.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A jester finds a fat <radical>jewel</radical> skewered on an iron rod in the vault. He hoists the rod overhead like a scepter. Everyone in the throne room bows to the new <kanji>king</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: When the king bellows for someone to open the shrine gates, the caretaker just grunts back <reading>おう</reading>, a lazy <reading>OW</reading> vowel flattened out of boredom, and shuffles off without a bow, unimpressed by royalty.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>ward</kanji> is the slice of city the council <radical>mow</radical>s off and seals inside its own <radical>hiding enclosure</radical>, so tax collectors know whose doors to knock on.
items.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Coo</reading>, the tax collector's pigeon, flies inside the sealed fence of each <kanji form="区">ward</kanji> the council mowed off, cooing 「<reading>く</reading>」 at every door his master must knock on.

items.meaning_mnemonic: <radical>Two hands</radical> stack <radical>one</radical> block, then <radical>two</radical> more on top. The wobbly pile tips down a <radical>slide</radical>. It crashes into <radical>three</radical> pieces and becomes a strange new <kanji>shape</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the sports field, coach <reading>Kay</reading> stares at the scratched-up chalk sketch and barks <reading>けい</reading> across the field, ordering everyone into position before the shape fades in the rain.

items.meaning_mnemonic: An <radical>old bird</radical> refuses to fly anymore. It hops off its perch onto the winding <radical>road</radical> below. Wings folded, it walks step by step to <kanji>advance</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Watching the bird finally waddle down the road, an old walker named <reading>Shin</reading> claps once and shouts <reading>しん</reading>, cheering it on like a marathon fan. He falls in behind it, refusing to walk any faster than the bird does.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>prefecture</kanji> is a region the capital thinks too <radical>small</radical> to visit, so it settles for keeping one <radical>hidden</radical> <radical>eye</radical> on it from far off.
items.reading_mnemonic: The capital sends <reading>Ken</reading> the sword-collecting dog as its one hidden eye on the small <kanji form="県">prefecture</kanji>, and he growls 「<reading>けん</reading>」 from far off at anyone who strays.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A foreman grips a loaded <radical>brush</radical>, ink dripping from its tip. He drags his back leg into a <radical>long stride or stretching</radical> that no real step should reach. The trailing brush inks one straight line, marking where to <kanji>build</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ken, the sword-collecting shiba, patrols the fresh foundation line like it is one more sword for his wall. Every lap he barks <reading>けん</reading>, and the crew swears the dog is shouting his own name, <reading>Ken</reading>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A surveyor measures exactly one <radical>inch</radical> beside each young <radical>tree</radical> she plants. She repeats it down the whole riverbank. The tidy row of measured trees becomes a little <kanji>village</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the riverbank, the surveyor's <reading>son</reading> grabs the ruler and marks a trunk crooked. She snaps his name flat across the water, <reading>そん</reading>, and he slinks off, apologizing for wrecking her careful measurements.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> beats down on a cracked garden box all day. Even so, <radical>ten</radical> thin blades of <radical>grass</radical> push through the dirt. The gardener gives up and lets the whole box run wild with <kanji>grass</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The gardener kneels by the windowbox and mutters <reading>そう</reading> under his breath with every seed he plants, like he's saying <reading>sow</reading> to himself out of habit. By the tenth blade, the word is stitched into the dirt.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The plaza of <radical>earth</radical> is held in high <radical>esteem</radical> by the whole town. A crowd fills it, too big for the open sky above. Someone stretches a giant <radical>cover</radical> across it, and it becomes the <kanji>public chamber</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Under the same blanket-roofed hall, a baker elbows in holding a fresh lump of <reading>dough</reading>, insisting the shrine crowd taste it. Everyone groans one long <reading>どう</reading>, half hunger, half surrender, and makes room for him anyway.
items.description: This kanji almost never stands alone. In real use it is nearly always the second half of a compound naming one specific large room — a dining hall, a lecture hall — rather than a generic public chamber on its own.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Toto the turtle sells a sample <radical>door</radical> that never stays shut. He chases it down every street as it swings open again and again. The whole town now knows him by that one runaway <kanji>door</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Outside that same konbini, Toto scrapes his shell along the loose sill trying to force a sale, and each scrape knocks out the same hollow sound: <reading>coh</reading>, <reading>こ</reading>. Shoppers wince every time but can't stop hearing it after they've left. Toto just shrugs it off as free advertising.

items.mnemonic_text: Two people standing side by side: to compare.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You get this one for free, because the <radical>compare</radical> radical and the <kanji>compare</kanji> kanji are the very same character, so it pays to know your radicals well.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the riverbank a heron named Hina lays two fish side by side to compare their weight. A jogger asks who landed the bigger one, so Hina jabs her beak toward the old fisherman, meaning <reading>he</reading> did, and croaks a flat <reading>ひ</reading> to settle it.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A city planner caps her model tower with a stone <radical>lid</radical>. Under it she props open a stone <radical>mouth</radical> as the gate. The whole model is so <radical>small</radical> it fits in her palm, a tiny <kanji>capital</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the ceremony, a boy named <reading>Kyo</reading> knocks the whole miniature capital off the table. It shatters on the floor, and all he can do is groan <reading>きょう</reading>, one long syllable of dread, as the tiny lid and gate pieces roll under the desks.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The furthest you can still make out a village by <radical>sun</radical>light is roughly one <kanji>ri</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The village elder who waves hikers toward the paddies goes by <reading>Lee</reading>. Every exhausted hiker calls back a grateful <reading>り</reading> as thanks. That's as much of his name as anyone manages out of breath. He just nods toward the shade.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>king</radical> wears a plain round crown of cheap glass beads. A single <radical>drop</radical> of dew lands on top and catches the light. Suddenly his crown looks like a real <kanji>jewel</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The royal jeweller <reading>Geo Cook</reading> leans in to inspect the new stone stuck to the king's crown. He raps it with a knuckle, and it rings glass-clear and true. He nods and stamps the papers <reading>ぎょく</reading>, the official reading for jewel, right on the spot.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A dog sheds a single strand of <radical>fur</radical> onto the porch. Wind lifts it and twists it into a tight curl. That stray curling strand is one piece of <kanji>fur</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the vending machine, a hiker named <reading>Moe</reading> picks the stray wisp off his sweaty arm for the third time this climb. He groans <reading>もう</reading>, long and tired, dragging the sound out like his own name stretched thin. Loose fur keeps finding him no matter how high he climbs.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A coin slips onto a <radical>slide</radical> and speeds toward the <radical>ground</radical>. A tiny <radical>barb</radical> flicks up and snags it just in time. That perfectly timed catch is pure <kanji>genius</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The hiker introduces himself as <reading>Sai</reading>, showing off his trick over and over. Everyone on the trail starts groaning <reading>さい</reading> before he even throws the coin, tired of his one genius party trick.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A monk drags a wooden marker across the bare <radical>earth</radical> to claim a plot. He measures it out with a tiny <radical>inch</radical> ruler, one stubborn tick at a time. By sundown the ring of stakes is wide enough for a <kanji>Buddhist temple</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The old groundskeeper everyone calls <reading>Jee</reading>, nobody remembers his real name, is the one who planted the signpost and paced out the whole plot with the inch ruler. Visitors greet him with a friendly <reading>じ</reading> before they even reach the gate. He's older than the temple itself now.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Two mountain slopes lean toward each other and pinch into a single <radical>valley</radical>. Rain runs down both sides and gathers in that low dip. It can never escape, so it fills the whole <kanji>valley</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the bottom, the hiker cracks open a can of <reading>coke</reading> and glugs it back with a throaty <reading>こく</reading>, foam sliding down her sleeve while the stone rolls to a stop at her boots.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>barley</radical> bows low in a strong wind. It keeps bending until its head touches the dirt. That endlessly bowing stalk is one tall shaft of <kanji>barley</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The farmer who tends that field introduces himself as <reading>Baku</reading>, bowing just like his crop. Everyone at the riverbank echoes <reading>ばく</reading> back at him, mimicking his stiff, grain-heavy bow every time he passes.

items.mnemonic_text: A dog (犬) squeezing back under a door (戸): to return.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Anything <radical>big</radical> enough to shove the never-latching <radical>door</radical> can <kanji>return</kanji> to the konbini heater whenever it wants.
items.reading_mnemonic: That big stray dog is called <reading>Ray</reading>. However many times Koichi shoos him out, the never-latching door swings open and lets him trot back past the onigiri shelf to the heater. Koichi just sighs <reading>れい</reading> and refills the food bowl.
items.description: The backtracking sense of return: going back where you were or putting something back, not returning home.

items.meaning_mnemonic: At the fair, a vendor yanks his <radical>arrow</radical> out of a ruined pumpkin. Its feathers still splay and the point is still sharp. He flings it at the fence instead and calls it a <kanji>dart</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back at the fair, Shea guards the fence where the runaway shaft first landed. Anyone who reaches for it too fast gets a sharp <reading>し</reading> — flat, quick, cutting the sentence off like a blade through pumpkin. It sounds exactly like her name, <reading>Shea</reading>, minus the vowel.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A kitten bats a ball of <radical>thread</radical> off the shelf. It bounces down every stair, unwinding as it falls. It lands in a knotted heap of <kanji>thread</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A seamstress named <reading>Shea</reading> catches the falling spool just before it hits the floor and hisses <reading>し</reading>, a long <reading>shh</reading>, so she doesn't wake the shop cat curled up in the thread bin.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A zookeeper plants two flags shaped like a <radical>chevron</radical> beside the panda pen. Overnight, each flagpole grows into a tall <radical>bamboo</radical> cane. The panda snaps off a whole clump of fresh <kanji>bamboo</kanji> to eat.
items.reading_mnemonic: Back on the schoolyard, a stray <reading>chick</reading> hops under the poles and pecks at the fallen bamboo leaves, cheeping <reading>ちく</reading> at every peck, until the coach finally shoos it off the field before practice starts.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A pirate buries a chest of <radical>money</radical> shells on the beach. High tide rolls in and buries it deeper every year. He digs it up decades later and finds only live <kanji>shellfish</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The coin-thief crow flaps off with a coin in its beak and caws <reading>ばい</reading>, sounding exactly like it's yelling <reading>bye</reading> over its shoulder. That's the reading you shout back at every shellfish it robs.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A cook grabs a long <radical>sword</radical> to slice open a stubborn bag of rice. The blade chips at the tip and bends sideways. He shrugs and keeps chopping with the bent <kanji>sword</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The clerk points and yells <reading>とう</reading>, sounding just like someone stubbing a <reading>toe</reading> on the counter, before confiscating the blade for scratching the onigiri shelf.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A curved stick strapped to a hunter's back is already shaped like a <radical>bow</radical>. She yanks the string until it hums with tension. It snaps forward and proves itself a true <kanji>bow</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A boy named <reading>Kyu</reading> lines up his shot on the sports field, and the string gives a sharp <reading>きゅう</reading> as it snaps back into place, leaving nothing but that one clean sound behind.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A startled duck yanks out a <radical>feather</radical> and it drifts onto the pond. The wind tugs more loose until dozens follow it down. Soon the whole pond is coated in floating <kanji>feathers</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The fisherman stares at his soggy catch and groans <reading>ooh</reading>, <reading>う</reading>, disgusted at wasting good bait on nothing but down. He flings the pair back toward the water, where the duck has already forgotten the whole ordeal and gone back to preening at the pond's edge.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Hot <radical>water</radical> bubbles under a crooked <radical>chevron</radical> roof. The heat turns it into swirling <radical>steam</radical>. It drifts into the cold air as <kanji>vapor</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki the tree spirit hides by the steaming pool and giggles at every gust. Cold spray hits her and she yelps <reading>き</reading>, sharp as a <reading>key</reading> turning in a lock, while the vapor drifts past her branch.
